attorneys.firm_name: Aiello Harris Abate Law Group, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Watchung, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Founding partner James A. Abate, Esq. chose to focus on criminal defense, DUI defense, and municipal court cases because, "Many people arrested for crimes have no previous experience with the law. They come from all walks of life, all ages, all professions, and are all genders. They need two things: They need to be educated, and they need a strong advocate." Mr. Abate's compassion for his clients is the driving force behind the firm. "Most importantly, what a client needs from me is knowing that everything is going to be okay. Bad decisions should not haunt you for the rest of your life." He supports his clients by giving them the information that they need to make hard decisions.

Mr. Abate says, "When you hire this firm, you get not just me, but an entire legal team dedicated to fighting for the best possible outcome in your case based on the facts and circumstances specific to your situation. Each member of our staff provides vital support for reaching successful resolutions."

He enjoys his Stanley Tucci-esq glasses and loves his sweet office puppy, Molly.

attorneys.name: Sally Abdulraouf Esq
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Palisades Park, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Sally Abdulraouf is an Associate Attorney at Kim, Lim & Partners, specializing in business litigation and commercial litigation. She earned her Juris Doctor from Rutgers Law School – Newark. She also holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in International Relations from American University of Sharjah in the UAE, as well as a Master’s degree in Political Sociology from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE). Prior to embarking on her legal career, Ms. Abdulraouf gained valuable international experience, having studied, worked, and lived in the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom. This global perspective informs her approach to legal practice and enhances her ability to provide counsel to clients in diverse sectors. She is also fluent in Arabic.

While at Rutgers Law, Ms. Abdulraouf was an active member of the Rutgers Journal of Law and Public Policy, serving as Managing Notes Editor. Her scholarly contributions were recognized with the prestigious Rutgers Law School Faculty Scholarship and Leadership Award, and her note titled “The Elections Transparency Act: A Step Backward For Fair And Democratic Elections In The Soprano State” was published in the Spring 2025 edition of the Journal (Volume 22, Issue 2). In addition, Ms. Abdulraouf was a member of the Entrepreneurship Clinic, where she assisted emerging businesses with a range of legal issues, and served as Co-Chair of the Women’s Law Forum, promoting the advancement of women in the legal field.

attorneys.firm_name: Sarno da Costa D'Aniello Maceri Webb LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Roseland, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Charles C. Abut is a Certified Matrimonial Attorney by the Supreme Court of New Jersey and a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers. Charles has successfully mediated and arbitrated hundreds of cases. He is a court-accredited mediator by the New Jersey Administrative Office of the Courts. He has also litigated a number of cases resulting in reported decisions, including Piscopo v. Piscopo, Rogers & Hammerstein v. Gilchinsky and Jacqueline Onassis v. Christian Dior. He has lectured for the New Jersey Judicial College and is a frequent lecturer for the New Jersey Institute of Continuing Education. Charles has published articles in the New Jersey Law Journal and New Jersey Lawyer, and has made television appearances on ABC, CBS, MSNBC and CNBC. He has been quoted in publications including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the Bergen Record. Prior to becoming an attorney, Charles was on active duty with the United States Army Military Police.

attorneys.name: Alfred V. Acquaviva, II, Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Hawthorne, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Alfred V. Acquaviva, II, Esq., is a licensed attorney in the State of New Jersey and the District Court of New Jersey, having successfully passed the New Jersey Bar Exam in July 2024. His areas of practice include civil litigation, commercial litigation, bankruptcy, representation of municipal entities and businesses, and sports and entertainment law.

Before becoming an attorney, Mr. Acquaviva gained valuable experience as a litigation paralegal at Acquaviva Law Offices, LLC, where he worked for 10 years. This extensive background provided him with a solid foundation in various areas of law and a deep understanding of client needs.

Alfred earned his Juris Doctor from Roger Williams University School of Law in 2024, where he was recognized with the "Outstanding Commitment to Pro Bono Legal Services" award for his dedication to community service. He received his undergraduate degree from Wagner College in 2018, graduating with a major in History and a minor in Business Administration, and was inducted into the Phi Alpha Theta National History Honor Society.

For the past six years, Alfred has served as the Passaic County Coordinator for the New Jersey High School Mock Trial Competition, a role in which he helps guide and mentor aspiring high school students with an interest in law.

Outside of his legal work, Alfred is an avid golfer and fisherman, and he enjoys spending time with his wife and their four dogs.

A member of the New Jersey State and Passaic County Bar Associations, Mr. Acquaviva is especially proud of his work with the New Jersey State Bar Association High School Mock Trial Committee for which he has been Passaic County Chair for fourteen (14) years.

attorneys.name: Kevork George Adanas
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Fort Lee, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Background & Scholarship

Mr. Adanas was born in Istanbul, Turkey and moved to the United States at the age of 5. Mr. Adanas graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in History cum laude from Providence College. He is a member Phi Alpha Theta International Honor Society, and earned a place on The National Deans' List for academic excellence. A talented tennis player in college, Mr. Adanas was named to the Big East Conference Academic All-Star Team in 1997 and 1997. He earned his Doctor of Jurisprudence degree from the Seton Hall University School of Law.

Education & Honors

Mr. Adanas graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in History from Providence College in 1997. He is a member Phi Alpha Theta International Honor Society, and earned a place on The National Deans' List for academic excellence. He earned his Doctor of Jurisprudence degree from the Seton Hall University School of Law in 2000.

Work Experience

While in law school, Mr. Adanas spent two summers clerking for Judge Daniel P. Mecca of the Bergen County Superior Court. He also gained valuable experience in commercial litigation, business and corporate law while serving as a clerk for the law firm of Aslanian & Khorozian, LLC.

Upon graduating, Mr. Adanas was retained as an associate attorney by Aslanian & Khorozian and was given the responsibility of full case management. It was here that he attained his expertise in commercial and corporate law. His proficiency was recognized in April 2002 when Mr. Adanas was offered the position of Managing Attorney in the New Jersey office of the law firm of Spiegel & Utrera, P.A. As office director, he oversaw the firm's practice of business and corporate law, immigration law, and issues of intellectual property.

Since July of 2005, Mr. Adanas has been the managing director of the Adanas Law Firm, focusing on Business, Corporate, Immigration matters and Real Estate law.

Professional Associations

Mr. Adanas' high level of knowledge and expertise is maintained and expanded upon through ongoing continuing legal education. He frequently attends nationally recognized conferences that intensely examine the latest legal decisions that may affect his clients.

Mr. Adanas is a member of the Business Law Section of the American Bar Association, New Jersey State Bar Association, and New York State Bar Association. He is also a member of the Trial Lawyers of America and the American Immigration Lawyers Association.

Court Admissions

Mr. Adanas is licensed to practice law before the United States Supreme Court, United States District Courts in the Southern District of New York, the Eastern District of New York, and in the District of New Jersey. He is also licensed to practice law in all courts in New Jersey, New York, and Washington D.C.

attorneys.name: Michael S. Adelman
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Defense in IRS Criminal Investigation (Federal, State, Local Tax Crimes Lawyers in Cherry Hill, NJ
attorneys.bio:
IRS, FEDERAL GRAND JURY, STATE TAX DEFENSE

If you are an individual, company, business or any other entity currently facing, or expecting to face, a criminal or civil tax investigation, you should immediately contact Michael S. Adelman, Esquire.

From 1970 through mid-1986, Mr. Adelman was employed in the IRS's Office of Regional Counsel, in Philadelphia, serving as a Senior Trial Attorney from 1975-1986.

During this 16-year service as an IRS attorney, Mr. Adelman was a specialist in the evaluation for the IRS of criminal tax (tax evasion, false returns, non-filing and Federal Grand Jury) matters. For seven of those years, he also represented the IRS in United States Tax Court civil cases, arising from appealed tax audits, usually involving issues such as unreported income, misstated deductions, civil fraud and/or other penalties, innocent spouse, tax shelters or transferee liability.

From mid-1986 to date, Mr. Adelman has moved to the "other side," with a legal practice geared almost exclusively to defense of Federal Tax crime investigations/charges. The range of services is from full-scale legal representation to consulting, serving as co-counsel or as an expert witness.

These tax defense services are available for tax evasion, non-filings, Federal Grand Jury, false tax returns and/or false statement Federal Tax cases. Mr. Adelman is also available for all issues typically involved in U.S. Tax Court cases, tax audits and administrative appeals from audit determinations, or for IRS collection disputes. Finally, Mr. Adelman has the expertise to offer counsel and representation in all types of State Tax disputes, especially for States located on the East Coast.

The tax defense services are not only for individuals and businesses, but also can be structured to assist accountants, or attorneys, who may wish to retain control of a client, while being guided and counseled behind-the-scenes by an expert with almost 48 years of tax controversy experience.

Finally, Mr. Adelman's tax practice is national in scope. Representation and counseling is available not only "in person," but by a combination of media such as phone, fax and e-mail. Advice can be rendered on an issue-by-issue or entire case basis.

Legal fees are reasonable, especially in light of Mr. Adelman's 16 years of compliance experience with the Treasury Department and almost five decades as a defense attorney. If you are an individual, company, business or any other entity currently facing, or expecting to face, a criminal or civil tax investigation, you should immediately contact Michael S. Adelman, Esquire.

For seven of those years, he also represented the IRS in United States Tax Court civil cases, arising from appealed tax audits, usually involving issues such as unreported income, misstated deductions, civil fraud and/or other penalties, innocent spouse, tax shelters or transferee liability.

attorneys.name: Joanna R. Adu Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills, Trusts and Estates Lawyers in Somerville, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Adu is a Shareholder and Partner at Lyons & Associates, where she chairs the firm’s Somerville office and Trusts, Estates, and Financial Practice Group. Her transactional practice includes wills, trusts and estates, guardianships, business law, non-profits, family office matters, and complex discovery issues. With the variety of her experience, Ms. Adu also regularly consults on complex firm cases involving special needs children and sophisticated assets.

Along with her legal practice, Ms. Adu is active in legal scholarship having co-authored the article “The Coming of Age of New Jersey Mental Health Courts: Addressing a Dilemma in the Criminal Justice System,” published in the February 2023 edition of New Jersey Lawyer, among other articles for various publications on topics such as estate planning for LGBTQ+ clients and posthumous litigation related to high-profile estates. She has also presented at professional conferences and other public events on topics such as basic estate planning, special needs planning, financial elder abuse, attorney ethics, pet custody, and more.

In her personal life, Ms. Adu is the proud parent of a child with special needs. As a special needs mom, she brings to her legal practice an innate understanding of the issues and concerns of special needs families, including providing for their future care. Her work and unique perspective as a special needs parent were highlighted in an individual profile in the 2023 New Jersey Super Lawyers magazine. She also currently serves on the Boards of Eden Autism Services and SERV Connect, two New Jersey non-profit organizations providing critical supports and services to individuals with special needs.

Ms. Adu has been recognized as a New Jersey Super Lawyers Rising Star in family law from 2020–2021, and in estate planning and probate law from 2022–2024.

Prior to joining Lyons & Associates, Ms. Adu completed a one-year clerkship for the Honorable Susan L. Reisner, P.J.A.D. (ret.). She earned her bachelor’s degree from the University of Washington and graduated cum laude from the Seattle University School of Law in 2016. She is admitted to practice in New Jersey and before the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey.

attorneys.practice_type: Commercial/Business Litigation Lawyers in Cherry Hill, NJ
attorneys.bio:
YooNieh Ahn is a well-rounded litigator with a wide range of experience in civil, criminal defense, and employment law. Prior to joining Hagner & Zohlman, she was an Associate at Jacobs & Barbone, a prominent boutique law firm in Atlantic City, where she first-chaired a sexual harassment case under New Jersey's Law Against Discrimination and obtained the largest settlement in the firm's history in a medical malpractice matter.

Prior to entering private practice, YooNieh served as Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable Max A. Baker, J.S.C. in Atlantic County, New Jersey. During her judicial clerkship, YooNieh became a certified mediator and mediated a variety of claims in small claims court.

YooNieh earned her Juris Doctor from Widener University, where she was a Senior Staff Member of the Widener Law Review and President of the Asian-Pacific American Law Students Association. She obtained a Bachelor of Arts in Economics from Boston University, where she graduated cum laude. YooNieh is licensed in New Jersey, the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey.

YooNieh is fluent in Korean. On her free time, she enjoys traveling, cooking and spending time with her husband and family.

attorneys.name: Christopher G. Aiello Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Aiello Harris Abate Law Group, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers In Criminal, Personal Injury & Employment Law Lawyers in Watchung, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Aiello has been engaged in litigation throughout his entire career that began in 1983. He has been honored with the top 100 trial attorney award in New Jersey by the national trial lawyers. He has achieved a 10.0 superb rating by Avvo a leading lawyer rating agency. His firm has been awarded a 5.0 out of 5.0 rating by Martindale Hubbell another leading lawyer rating group.

He has appeared in dozens of televised, print and internet media including: New York Post, New York Daily News, the Newark Star-Ledger, the Bergen Record, the Philadelphia Inquirer, NJ.com, News 12 New Jersey, ABC, NBC, CBS, CBS Radio, 101.5 FM, WINS Radio New York, etc. He initially worked a well-known insurance defense firm where he served as defense counsel for insurance companies and large corporations including the Chrysler Corporation, the Hertz Corporation, Mitsubishi motors, Stanley tools, and medical professionals involved in medical malpractice cases. Mr. Aiello then took this intensive background and training and began representing people as plaintiffs in personal injury and employment litigation matters. He also since he was a former municipal prosecutor represented people in need of criminal defense. He and his team of attorneys have achieved substantial results for their clients.

Personal Injury Case Examples:

A 7.4 million structured settlement for a wrongful death of a child and an emotional distress claim for the mother and sister.

A $1.4 million settlement for wrongful death suit as a result of excessive force at a hotel.

A $900,000 settlement when a man suffered a cervical fusion when he was involved in a car accident.

A $1.4 million settlement for racial discrimination.

A $450,000 settlement when a woman was sexually harassed, a $300,000 settlement for a person who was a whistleblower.

Employment Law Case Examples:

Murray vs. Orleans Construction. $7.4 million. Structured settlement.

Jacobson vs. Lake Mohawk. $2.2 million settlement. Diving accident and medical malpractice.

Kondratyk vs. Holiday Inn. $1.4 million. Wrongful death negligence with excessive force.

Kelly vs. Sands Hotel and Casino. $750,000. Fall down on wet floor resulting in injuries.

Russo vs. Morgan. $900,000

Hernandez vs. Jones. $450,000

Criminal Law Case Examples:

Police charge defendant with possession of a handgun and purchasing drugs. If the defendant is found guilty it is an automatic state prison sentence. He filed a motion to suppress due to and illegal search and seizure by the police resulting in all criminal charges being dismissed.

Third offense DUI found not guilty. Mr. Aiello proved that although the vehicle was running the defendant did not have the requisite intent to operate a motor vehicle. Mr. Aiello’s efforts resulted in the defendant avoiding 180 days in jail and 10 years loss of driving privileges.

Young man denied Pre-trial intervention program. The allegations were that the defendant was dealing drugs to undercover officers. The trial judge agreed with Mr. Aiello and admitted the defendant into the program. The prosecutor appealed the decision to the Appellate Division . Mr. Aiello wrote a brief in opposition and the Appellate Division agreed with his position. Again, the prosecutor appealed to the Supreme Court and once again the Supreme Court agreed with the defendants and Mr. Aiello’s position and he was admitted into the program.

Defendant had a gun and committed a first-degree robbery. He could have received a prison sentence between 10 to 20 years while serving 85% of the time under (NERA) The no early release act. The plea offer was originally 12 years. Mr. Aiello negotiated with the prosecutor resulting in a second-degree sentence of five years. He then made a motion to the sentencing judge to treat the defendant as a 3rd degree offender and not a 2nd degree offender. That motion was granted and the defendant’s sentence was reduced to three years. If you are charged with a crime please contact Mr. Aiello and his team of criminal trial attorneys.

In regards to criminal law, motions to dismiss resulting in acquittals for the defendant, motions to suppress resulting in acquittals for the defendant, negotiating excellent plea-bargain for defendants and wins at the appellate division for criminal defendants.

If you need experienced and tough litigators contact Mr. Aiello and his team of attorneys.

He practices in the Superior Court of New Jersey in both the trial court section and the appellate divisions, the Workers’ Compensation Court, and Municipal Courts.

attorneys.name: Francesca Aiello
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury- Plaintiffs Lawyers in Fort Lee, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Francesca Nicholas is a Partner and trial lawyer of the Law Offices Rosemarie Arnold representing injured parties in areas of personal injury, employment discrimination and specializing in cases dealing with catastrophic injuries.

Francesca graduated from Fordham University, Bronx, New York in 1993 earning her Bachelor of Arts in Sociology with a concentration in criminal justice. During the last two years of college, she worked at the Bergen County Sheriff’s Department and assisted in coordinating assignments for work release inmates.

Francesca graduated from Quinnipiac University School of Law in 1997 earning her Juris Doctor degree. After law school, Francesca completed a Judicial Clerkship from 1997-1998 with the Honorable Lawrence D. Smith, Ret. J.S.C. in the Superior Court of New Jersey, Bergen County. She was admitted to practice law in the State of New Jersey and the Federal Courts of New Jersey in January of 1998.

After completing her yearlong Judicial Clerkship, Francesca practiced law for five years in a small personal injury firm in Clifton, New Jersey where she actively tried cases.

Francesca joined the Law Offices Rosemarie Arnold as an Associate and trial lawyer in June of 2003. She has successfully tried cases in many counties in the State of New Jersey and has also successfully settled cases vigorously advocating for her clients.

On a personal note, Francesca is a long time resident of Bergen County since the age of 4 where she and her husband are raising two children, and is fluent in Italian.

attorneys.name: Paul N. Ambrose
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Hackensack, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Paul N. Ambrose, Jr. chairs the New Jersey firm's office of estate planning, estate litigation and tax practice. Mr. Ambrose has concentrated his practice in the following areas of the law: Corporate law, Taxation, Trusts & Estates, Real Estate, Franchise law, Internal Revenue Service disputes both civil and criminal, Probate and Estate litigation, Commercial transactions and litigation.

Interaction with taxing authorities can be both distressing and unsettling. Mr. Ambrose has represented clients in a variety of matters before the Internal Revenue Service, Division of Taxation of New Jersey and Department of Labor. He is committed to protecting the financial and legal interests of the firm's clients facing those taxing authorities. Mr. Ambrose works directly with our firm's clients in conjunction with accountants, former Internal Revenue Services' Agents and specialists, to create a tax team that focuses their efforts on strategic and tactical decisions at the onset of an inquiry to assist the clients in avoiding or minimizing tax exposure.

Mr. Ambrose has represented proponents and contestants of wills and litigated a wide variety of issues in probate and estate litigation. He has been involved in preparing estate plans, including Wills, Insurance Trusts, Living Wills, Advance Medical Directives, Personal Residence Trusts, Durable Powers of Attorney, Revocable Living Trusts, Family Limited Partnerships or Limited Liability Companies.

Mr. Ambrose has extensive experience with all areas of franchise and distributorship litigation and dispute resolution, representing numerous franchisors and franchisees and distributors and distributees. Whether negotiating a franchise agreement, litigating a distributor termination, or drawing up franchise business plans, Mr. Ambrose can provide professional services to his clients.

Mr. Ambrose was counsel to the noncustodial spouse in the seminal family law case regarding joint de facto custody after the New Jersey Supreme Court relaxed the law for custodial parents to relocate entitle, O'Connor vs. O'Connor, 349 N.J. Super. 381 (App. Div. 2002)

attorneys.name: Terrance W. Annese
attorneys.firm_name: Weinberger Divorce & Family Law Group, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Alimony Lawyers in Mount Laurel, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Terrance W. Annese is an attorney at Weinberger Divorce & Family Law Group, LLC. with nearly three decades of experience providing highly skilled and effective legal representation in divorce and family law matters. Terrance focuses on securing favorable outcomes for clients in cases involving divorce, child custody, alimony, child support, equitable distribution, domestic violence, and related family issues.

Terrance’s passion for family law began during his studies at The Catholic University of America – Columbus School of Law, where he worked in the Families and the Law Clinic advocating for underrepresented clients in the Washington, DC area. This formative experience ignited his career-long passion for helping individuals and families find stability in times of upheaval.

“In guiding my clients through the chaos, confusion and fear of the unknown, in what are often the most difficult personal and intimate challenges of their lives, my goal is to protect my clients’ interests, resolve disputes efficiently, and achieve outcomes that allow them to move forward with confidence and peace of mind,” Terrance explains.

Clients trust Terrance to take decisive action and develop strategic solutions tailored to their unique situation and needs, breaking down even the most complicated matters into a clear, actionable “road map” towards their goals. At every step, Terrance ensures his clients feel informed, confident, and fully supported.

Whether negotiating settlements or advocating in court, Terrance remains focused on delivering meaningful results that safeguard his clients’ rights and secure their long-term well-being. While Terrance prioritizes low-conflict resolutions to reduce stress and encourage positive outcomes, he is fully prepared to pursue litigation aggressively when necessary. His blend of assertive advocacy and practical problem-solving ensures that his clients’ goals are achieved.

After earning his Juris Doctorate, Terrance served as a New Jersey Superior Court Law Clerk to the late Honorable Thomas DeMartin, P.J. Criminal Part. In this role, he gained valuable insight into how judges assess cases, an insider’s perspective that he now uses to position his clients for success in court. Additionally, he had the opportunity to assist in several high-profile cases, including the nation’s first Megan’s Law classifications.

Following his clerkship, Terrance served as a Deputy Attorney General with the New Jersey Department of Law and Public Safety for nine years. In this role, he tackled a wide array of legal duties, from enforcing state laws to providing legal advice to state agencies. This background in public service sharpened his ability to resolve legal issues with precision and effectively protect his clients’ interests.

Terrance is licensed to practice before the New Jersey and Pennsylvania courts and is a proud member of the New Jersey State Bar Association (NJSBA), including the NJSBA’s Family Law Section, as well as the Pennsylvania State Bar Association. He is also a member of the Burlington, Camden and Ocean County Bar Associations.

A native of West Paterson, New Jersey, Terrance earned his undergraduate degree from Rutgers University – Newark College of Arts & Sciences. He now resides in Southern New Jersey, where he enjoys caring for his three miniature schnauzers and pursuing his passion for thoroughbred horse racing in which he has been a licensed owner in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Maryland. He is also an avid fan of competitive sports, including baseball, hockey, and football.

Before practicing law, Terrance was a semi-pro baseball player, earning a walk-on acting role as a baseball player in the 1994 film, Major League II. Terrance also ran his own men’s semi-pro baseball team for more than two decades.

Born in Camden, New Jersey in 1961, Mr. Antinori currently resides in Voorhees Township.

attorneys.name: Michael Aquino
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Paterson, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Michael Aquino worked to pay his way through college and law school and is the first person in his family to have graduated from college. After graduating SUNY Stony Brook, with honors in 1983, he went to Brooklyn Law School and competed in the Moot Court Trial and was privileged to win the Sidney Talmadge individual award for trial excellence. He graduated from Brooklyn Law in 1986, and passed both the New Jersey and New York Bar examinations on his first attempt. He was hired as an attorney by the Manhattan insurance defense firm where he previously worked as a law clerk. There, he successfully tried multiple bodily injury cases gaining substantial experience in defense strategies and tactics. Afterward, he joined one of the largest and most prominent law firms in New Jersey and litigated one of the largest environmental cases as well as complex construction defect claims, bodily injury lawsuits, and commercial disputes.

In 1995, Michael joined Salomon & Blackman, which has been representing the injured in Bergen and Passaic County since 1962. The firm is now called Salomon & Aquino, but the guiding philosophy is the same: we do what is right for you. He is a member of the Passaic County Bar Association and the New Jersey Bar Association. Michael brings 30 years of transactional, litigation and trial experience to the firm. Perhaps more importantly, he understands the tremendous emotional and financial burden that being injured in an accident can cause on a person's life and has developed methods to aggressively and swiftly achieve solid results for his clients.

attorneys.name: Anthony M. Arbore
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Netcong, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Anthony M. Arbore is a Partner of Arbore Velez, LLC and has been practicing law in Morris County with the firm for more than 30 years. He became a member of the New Jersey State Bar in 1985 and a named Partner in the predecessor firm of Forster & Arbore only 4 years thereafter. Mr. Arbore’s practice focuses primarily on criminal and civil trial litigation, as well as DWI defense, and the representation of public employee’s throughout the State of New Jersey on disciplinary matters. His practice consists of handling numerous types of matters on behalf of his clients, such as automobile accidents, various types of personal injury actions, slip-and-fall cases, defective product litigation, as well as complex commercial litigation. In addition to DWI defense, Mr. Arbore handles all aspects of Municipal Court proceedings as well as the defense of juveniles in Superior Court. Mr. Arbore’s significant experience and familiarity with various local Court systems and procedures, both as a Municipal Prosecutor for more than 24 years and as a defense attorney during that period of time, enables him to provide invaluable advice and representation to his clients in each of the matters he handles on their behalf.

In his years as a litigator, Mr. Arbore has handled a number of high profile criminal matters as well as many notable police and other public employee disciplinary matters. He has successfully argued cases in the Appellate Courts of this State and also successfully argued a controversial and significant juvenile rights case before the Supreme Court of the State of New Jersey in 2005. Mr. Arbore has been counsel of record in four published decisions of New Jersey’s Appellate Courts.

Mr. Arbore is a member of the New Jersey State Bar Association, the Morris County Bar Association and the American Bar Association, as well as a member of the Trial Attorney’s of New Jersey, the Association of Trial Lawyer’s of America, New Jersey Chapter, and the Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys. He also served as Co-Chairman of the Morris County Bar Association Municipal Court Committee in 2009 and currently holds this position for 2010. He is a Certified Municipal Prosecutor. Among his significant number of appointments as a Municipal Prosecutor, he currently holds the position with the following Municipalities: Byram Township, Hopatcong Borough and Andover Township. He also previously served the following Municipalities as Municipal Prosecutor: Chester Township, Netcong Borough, Sussex Borough, Vernon Township, and also as Special Prosecutor in Jefferson Township. Additionally, Mr. Arbore currently serves as the Sussex County Municipal Prosecutor Liaison to the New Jersey State Municipal Prosecutor's Association. He is also an approved PBA Attorney for New Jersey. Mr. Arbore is a Certified Morris County Superior Court Arbitrator and has also formerly held the positions of Secretary and President of the Morris County Municipal Prosecutor’s Association.

Mr. Arbore graduated Seton Hall University Magna Cum Laude with a degree in Criminal Justice/Sociology. While at Seton Hall University Mr. Arbore was named to the International Sociology Honor Society. Upon graduation he was the sole recipient of the prestigious Honor of Outstanding Academic Achievement in the major of Criminal Justice. Mr. Arbore is also a graduate of the Seton Hall University School of Law where he graduated Cum Laude.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mountainside, NJ
attorneys.bio:
A Family Law Litigator & Qualified as a State of New Jersey Mediator

Jodi Argentino has 23 years of experience practicing as a litigator in New Jersey and is Qualified as a State of New Jersey Family Law Mediator. She strives to ensure clients receive comprehensive legal representation based on their needs in a timely, efficient manner. Jodi prides herself on developing creative solutions and thinking "outside the box." She has developed her practice to form a holistic, candid environment for advocacy and real life practical solutions.

Jodi takes an active role in her hometown and in the LGBTQ community.

Jodi is an advocate of staying true to oneself despite adversity, echoing George Eliot's words, "It is never too late to be what you might have been."

Areas of practice and interest

Jodi handles all types of family law cases and has a special interest in:

LGBT-specific Family Law

Complex Parentage Litigation

Psychological/De Facto Parentage

Family Formation

Jurisdictional and Multistate Litigation

Mediation

Multi-parent families

Adoption

Artificial Reproductive Technology Law

Jodi is an invited member of the Family Law Institute of the National LGBT Bar Association, a vetted group of family lawyers from across the country with significant experience in LGBT family law matters, a member of the Board of Trustees of the NJSBA LGBT Section, and a lecturer on LGBT issues in New Jersey and nationally. Jodi is also a partner of LGBTeach, LLC, an organization providing cultural competency and diversity training.

attorneys.name: Jennifer D. Armstrong
attorneys.practice_type: Living Wills Lawyers in Toms River, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Diane Armstrong is the founding member of the firm, Jennifer D. Armstrong, LLC a full service family law firm dedicated to helping people protect their wealth during a divorce so that they can become happier and more successful. The firm was established in October of 2007 and is located in Toms River, New Jersey.

Jennifer has devoted herself to helping individuals successfully close one chapter of their lives and move on to the next. Our firm is enthusiastic in changing the way individuals view divorce. For some divorce can seem overwhelming and the process emotionally and financially draining but it doesn't have to be. The firm is committed to assisting our clients in becoming more knowledgeable about their options, determining what options best suits the client's needs and that of their family and moving forward. Our belief is that your divorce or family law matter does not have to define you, it is not who you are but one moment in time on your way to a happier and more successful life.

Jennifer was born and raised in New Jersey and is a graduate of Stockton University and Widener University School of Law. Jennifer has been practicing family law since 2002.

Jennifer is a member of the New Jersey State Bar Association Family Law Section, the Ocean County Bar Association Family Law Committee and Women's Committee, a panelist for the Ocean County Bar Matrimonial Early Settlement Panel program and a panel member on the Supreme Court of New Jersey District IIIA Fee Arbitration Committee. Jennifer is admitted to practice law in the State of New Jersey and is admitted and qualified as an Attorney and Counselor of the Supreme Court of the United States.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Lee, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Rosemarie Arnold was born on June 9, 1962 to Iris Arnold, a school teacher, and Dr. Murray Arnold, an obstetrician gynecologist. Her dad passed away when she was 5 years old, leaving her mother to raise their 6 children in Washington Heights, New York. She graduated with honors from the Bronx High School of Science in 1979, where she was the captain of the women's swim team. In 1983, at age 20, Arnold graduated from The State University of New York at Binghamton, then headed to Brooklyn Law School where she was a member of the Moot Court Honor Society and captain of the negotiating team.

After graduating from law school in 1986, Arnold began her career at the Law Offices of Christian Stueben, where she represented predominantly large corporate defendants, such as Foodtown, Pathmark, Stop & Shop, Campbell's Soup Company, Arcola Bus Company, Bally’s Total Fitness, T.G.I. Fridays, Libby’s Foods and Cigna Insurance Company.

In 1989, feeling unfulfilled with defense litigation, Arnold founded The Law Offices Rosemarie Arnold, (a firm devoted to the representation of injured victims), in a one room office in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey which she shared with her paralegal Mary Mazza. Thirty-six years later, Arnold has built her law firm into one of the largest and most successful injury law firms of New Jersey where Mary Mazza served as the COO until her retirement in 2021.

Between 1989 and the present, Law Offices Rosemarie Arnold has recovered over a billion dollars in settlements and judgments for their grateful clients and succeeded in scores of high-profile cases.

As an injury lawyer of New Jersey, Arnold has been called upon to give her legal expertise to the NY Times, Daily News, New York Post and Wall Street Journal. She has also appeared as a legal expert on Good Morning America, the Today Show, The Early Show, Maury Povich, NY1, ABC, NBC, CBS and FOX News, Inside Edition, and Extra TV. Notably in 2013, Arnold was named EXTRA TV’s legal correspondent.

Arnold has been bestowed with many accolades and honors including:

Arnold is admitted to the bars of New Jersey, New York and Nevada. She is also admitted to the United States District Court of New Jersey, the United States Eastern District Court of New York and the United States Southern District of New York.

Arnold is a member of the Multimillion Dollar Advocates Club, Bergen County Bar Association, New Jersey Bar Association, New York Bar Association, Nevada Bar Association and the American Association for Justice.

Arnold sits on the Board of Trustees of the Rebeka Verea Foundation, a non-profit corporation founded in the memory of a 17 year old client of Arnold’s who was killed on the night of her high school graduation, while a passenger in a speeding car. Arnold also sits on the Board of Trustees of the Leonard Melfi Foundation.

Arnold sat on the Board of Education of Saddle River in an elected position from 2006 to 2015.

Arnold has been profiled in several periodicals including New Jersey Super Lawyers, Social Life Magazine, The Bergen Record and The Town Journal.

Arnold has made recent headlines for her extraordinary results on behalf of sexual abuse victims.

attorneys.name: Carolann M. Aschoff
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Jersey City, NJ
attorneys.bio:
The firm of Carolann M. Aschoff, P.C., began in l994. Prior to that, Carolann Aschoff had worked for and subsequently became a partner in a general practice firm for nine years. She handled most of the matrimonial matters for that firm, and when the partnership dissolved she decided to open up her own firm with the express purpose of concentrating in and focusing on family matters in the law.

She has dedicated her professional career to developing a matrimonial firm that is committed to giving clients professional, compassionate and comprehensive services to assist them during a difficult period in their lives. She received the Matrimonial Attorney of the Year from the Hudson County Bar Association in 2002. Her commitment is found not only in her dedication and hard work in this field of law, but also in the professionally trained staff that have been with the firm for several years. The associate attorneys working at the firm are skilled practitioners who fully appreciate the importance of providing the highest quality of service to each and every client and to that end regularly attend continuing legal education seminars along with Carolann to keep up with new trends in the law that will impact their clients. The administrative/secretarial staff has been with the firm for many years and fully support and facilitate the firm's credo of personal attention to each and every client. The legal support staff offers comprehensive research and writing skills to assist each attorney in the firm to produce a quality work product designed to advance the best interests of each client.

This firm stands for quality service and strong representation. It is also mindful of the emotional and psychological experiences of each client and the right of each client to receive the personal attention they deserve. The law firm of Carolann M. Aschoff, P.C., is here to provide a strong legal port in the storm of each client's life at a time when it is needed.

Carolann M. Aschoff has been designated by the Supreme Court of New Jersey as a Certified Matrimonial Law Attorney. Less than 2% of New Jersey lawyers are Certified Matrimonial Law Attorneys. Carolann M. Aschoff has also been appointed by courts as a guardian and parent coordinator.

attorneys.name: Rebecca S. Ashkenazi
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Union, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Ashkenazi is a Partner at Wolfenson & Ashkenazi, P.C. Her current practice focuses on Real Estate matters, Wills, Trusts, and Estates (including Probate matters), as well as Guardianships. She regularly handles complex transactions and estate matters with a practical, client-centered approach, guiding individuals and families through significant financial and personal decisions. Ms. Ashkenazi also represents clients in guardianship proceedings and has been appointed by the Court to serve as counsel for alleged incapacitated individuals, a role she approaches with particular care and a strong sense of responsibility to protect the rights and dignity of vulnerable persons.

Prior to focusing on real estate and estate planning, her practice was dedicated to representing abandoned, abused, and neglected children, as well as working on high-net-worth matrimonial matters. That experience continues to inform her work today, bringing a thoughtful and empathetic perspective to matters that are often deeply personal. She found this area of practice especially meaningful, and she believes that work helps her to continue to support clients through important life transitions while helping to secure and protect their futures.

Ms. Ashkenazi has been named one of New Jersey's "Best Lawyers for Families" by NJ Family Magazine for four consecutive years, an award earned through client nominations. She has also received the “Client’s Choice Award” for six consecutive years on Avvo.com. She looks forward to continuing to provide her clients with the highest level of service.

Ms. Ashkenazi has been working with Urban Dance League, Inc. since 2013 in both a legal capacity and a board member-style role, providing guidance and direction for new ideas and opportunities. Urban Dance League not only creates a platform for dancers but also creates programs and safe spaces for children which is extremely important to Ms. Ashkenazi.

At Franklin and Marshall College, Ms. Ashkenazi was a co-founder of S.I.S.T.E.R.S (Sophisticated, Intelligent, Sisters, Teaching, Excellence, Responsibility, and Success), an organization that has been active for more than 20 years and, she notes with pride, has grown to more than 10x its original size since its inception. S.I.S.T.E.R.S is an organization that promotes intelligence, empowerment, and unity among women and Ms. Ashkenazi is still involved with current and alumni members.

attorneys.name: Robert A. Assuncao
attorneys.practice_type: National Trial Practice Lawyers in East Brunswick, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Assuncao advises current and future market leading corporations concerning risk management, litigation and product development issues. Mr. Assuncao's diverse national litigation practice includes the representation of corporations in a wide variety of complex commercial, class action, product liability, and toxic tort cases. Mr. Assuncao also advises clients concerning the regulatory compliance of product labels. He has represented manufacturers in product liability actions for over 25 years at the trial and appellate level. He serves as national trial and class action counsel for one of the world's largest consumer product manufacturers and class action counsel for a global consumer electronics company.

Mr. Assuncao is a member of the state bars of New Jersey, New York and Colorado. He is also admitted to practice in the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey, the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Districts of New York, the District of Colorado, the Federal Court of Claims, the Eastern District of Michigan, the United States Courts of Appeals for the Second and Third Circuits, and the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Assuncao is a Sustaining Member of the Product Liability Advisory Council and a member of the Defense Research Institute. Mr. Assuncao is rated AV® PreeminentTM 5.0 out of 5 by the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory.

Mr. Assuncao has litigated matters in a number of jurisdictions throughout the United States and Canada and has significant experience with different forms of alternative dispute resolution.

Mr. Assuncao, a founding partner of Ansa Assuncao LLP, has received the distinguished honor of being selected as one of New York’s Top Rated Lawyers by the publication issued by ALM Media and Martindale-Hubbell.

Representative Experience:

Counsel for British manufacturer of industrial machinery before the United States Supreme Court, in a case that the Court, for the first time in 24 years, addressed a corporate defendant's liberty right to be free from personal jurisdiction in a state where the defendant had no deliberate contacts. In the matter, the Court reversed the New Jersey Supreme Court's improper and unconstitutional exercise of personal jurisdiction over the corporate defendant.

Corporate and Litigation Counsel for a generic pharmaceutical company.

National Counsel for leading international coatings manufacturer in all forms of litigation and labeling issues.

Counsel for a global electronics manufacturer in several putative class actions, filed in several states related to certain high definition televisions.

Counsel for national seller of hardware in defense of an alleged $40 million breach of contract claim brought by manufacturer based in Taiwan and mainland China. A business solution to the dispute was negotiated to the satisfaction of both parties.

Counsel for billing aggregator in a putative class action alleging the aggregator placed unauthorized, misleading, or deceptive charges (also known as "cramming") on telephone bills. After investigation of the charges, we convinced the claimants that their claims were without merit and to dismiss the claim.

Counsel for a global electronics manufacturer in a putative national consumer class action alleging consumer fraud and unjust enrichment claims related its LED high definition televisions. The case was dismissed on a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss.

Appellate Counsel for a global manufacturer of automobiles before the New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division on appeal from a defense verdict at trial. The New Jersey Appellate Court affirmed the trial court verdict on all issues.

Counsel for an international manufacturer of plumbing fixtures in a case in New York Supreme Court involving catastrophic injuries to an infant. The case dismissed with prejudice on motion for summary judgment at trial and the dismissal was affirmed by the New York Appellate Division, Second Department.

Counsel for international manufacturer of motorcycles in wrongful death action alleging that the manufacturer improperly marketed racing motorcycles to ordinary riders for street use. Granting a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss, the court dismissed plaintiff's design defect claims finding that the speed and lightweight nature of the manufacturer's motorcycles are performance features and not defects as a matter of law.

Counsel for a global electronics manufacturer in a putative national consumer class action alleging breach of warranty, consumer fraud, and unjust enrichment claims related to its DLP high definition televisions. The case was dismissed on a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss.

Counsel for a leading international plumbing fixture fitting manufacturer in a putative consumer class action asserting strict liability, breach of warranty, and negligence claims related to certain tub and shower valves. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed their claims with prejudice in response to defendants' opposition to class certification and cross motion to strike plaintiffs' experts.

Counsel for an international manufacturer of microwave ovens in a putative national consumer class action. The case was dismissed on a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss.

Counsel for a national lumber retailer in a putative state consumer class action related to pressure treated lumber.

Counsel for a reinsurance broker in $40 million reinsurance underwriting and fraud litigation.

Counsel for National Football League franchise in litigation involving its stadium alcohol policies that attracted national media attention.

Counsel for a securities trading company, securities brokers and an attorney in a putative class action lawsuit alleging fraud, breach of fiduciary duty, and violations of NJRICO.

Counsel for an ASME code inspection agency and insurance company in successful appeal before United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.

Counsel in defense of a national class action lawsuit in Texas, involving a claim that, over a ten-year period, the client manufactured more than three million defective water heaters. Plaintiffs alleged damages in excess of $1 billion. The trial court certified three national classes. However, class certification was defeated at the appellate level. Plaintiffs' petitions for certification to the Texas Supreme Court were denied, and, upon remand, the case was dismissed in its entirety by the trial court.

Counsel for a manufacturer of water heaters in eight consumer class action lawsuits brought in Alabama, California, Illinois, Kansas, Michigan (two cases), Missouri, and Tennessee. These cases involved an allegedly defective water heater component called a dip tube which, upon failure, could damage the heater and the home's plumbing system.

Counsel for British manufacturer of industrial machinery before the United States Supreme Court, in a case that the Court, for the first time in 24 years, addressed a corporate defendant's liberty right to be free from personal jurisdiction in a state where the defendant had no deliberate contacts. In the matter, the Court reversed the New Jersey Supreme Court's improper and unconstitutional exercise of personal jurisdiction over the corporate defendant.

Corporate and Litigation Counsel for a generic pharmaceutical company.

National Counsel for leading international coatings manufacturer in all forms of litigation and labeling issues.

Counsel for a global electronics manufacturer in several putative class actions, filed in several states related to certain high definition televisions.

Counsel for national seller of hardware in defense of an alleged $40 million breach of contract claim brought by manufacturer based in Taiwan and mainland China. A business solution to the dispute was negotiated to the satisfaction of both parties.

Counsel for billing aggregator in a putative class action alleging the aggregator placed unauthorized, misleading, or deceptive charges (also known as "cramming") on telephone bills. After investigation of the charges, we convinced the claimants that their claims were without merit and to dismiss the claim.

Counsel for a global electronics manufacturer in a putative national consumer class action alleging consumer fraud and unjust enrichment claims related its LED high definition televisions. The case was dismissed on a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss.

Appellate Counsel for a global manufacturer of automobiles before the New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division on appeal from a defense verdict at trial. The New Jersey Appellate Court affirmed the trial court verdict on all issues.

Counsel for an international manufacturer of plumbing fixtures in a case in New York Supreme Court involving catastrophic injuries to an infant. The case dismissed with prejudice on motion for summary judgment at trial and the dismissal was affirmed by the New York Appellate Division, Second Department.

Counsel for international manufacturer of motorcycles in wrongful death action alleging that the manufacturer improperly marketed racing motorcycles to ordinary riders for street use. Granting a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss, the court dismissed plaintiff's design defect claims finding that the speed and lightweight nature of the manufacturer's motorcycles are performance features and not defects as a matter of law.

Counsel for a global electronics manufacturer in a putative national consumer class action alleging breach of warranty, consumer fraud, and unjust enrichment claims related to its DLP high definition televisions. The case was dismissed on a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss.

Counsel for a leading international plumbing fixture fitting manufacturer in a putative consumer class action asserting strict liability, breach of warranty, and negligence claims related to certain tub and shower valves. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed their claims with prejudice in response to defendants' opposition to class certification and cross motion to strike plaintiffs' experts.

Counsel for an international manufacturer of microwave ovens in a putative national consumer class action. The case was dismissed on a 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss.

Counsel for a national lumber retailer in a putative state consumer class action related to pressure treated lumber.

Counsel for a reinsurance broker in $40 million reinsurance underwriting and fraud litigation.

Counsel for National Football League franchise in litigation involving its stadium alcohol policies that attracted national media attention.

Counsel for a securities trading company, securities brokers and an attorney in a putative class action lawsuit alleging fraud, breach of fiduciary duty, and violations of NJRICO.

Counsel for an ASME code inspection agency and insurance company in successful appeal before United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.

Counsel in defense of a national class action lawsuit in Texas, involving a claim that, over a ten-year period, the client manufactured more than three million defective water heaters. Plaintiffs alleged damages in excess of $1 billion. The trial court certified three national classes. However, class certification was defeated at the appellate level. Plaintiffs' petitions for certification to the Texas Supreme Court were denied, and, upon remand, the case was dismissed in its entirety by the trial court.

Counsel for a manufacturer of water heaters in eight consumer class action lawsuits brought in Alabama, California, Illinois, Kansas, Michigan (two cases), Missouri, and Tennessee. attorneys.name: Francine Aster Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family and Matrimonial Law Lawyers in Livingston, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Francine Aster Esq., is a Partner at Ziegler Law Group LLC, and a seasoned family law attorney with a strong track record of success and client trust. Her practice is devoted exclusively to family and matrimonial law, with extensive experience in areas such as divorce, domestic violence, custody disputes, grandparent visitation, child and spousal support, equitable distribution of assets, adoptions, paternity matters, prenuptial agreements, palimony, alimony, mediation, post-judgment enforcement and modification, and other related issues. She is also certified by the New Jersey courts as an approved mediator.

Francine’s dedication to family law stems from her deep-rooted commitment to helping others. She is known for her personal and proactive approach to client service. Francine listens closely to her clients’ goals and concerns, making herself available and responsive throughout every step of the legal process. Her clients appreciate her steady guidance, prompt communication, and her ability to bring clarity and comfort during uncertain times.

Francine brings a wealth of knowledge to every case, allowing her to develop innovative legal strategies, particularly in contentious or complex matters. Whether resolving issues through negotiation, mediation, or litigation, she tailors her approach to best suit each client’s unique circumstances and is a fierce advocate from start to finish.

Child custody is one of Francine’s particular areas of focus. Her deep understanding of the law is enhanced by her experience serving as a guardian ad litem (GAL), where she assists courts in determining custody arrangements that serve the best interests of the child. She has also acted as a court-appointed parenting coordinator and parenting supervisor, equipping her with insight into managing conflict and supporting cooperative co-parenting.

An active and respected leader within the New Jersey family law community, Francine volunteers with the Matrimonial Early Settlement Panels (ESPs) in Essex and Morris Counties, helping couples reach informed settlement decisions. Through her longstanding role with Volunteer Lawyers for Justice (VLJ), she has taught divorce law basics at the Essex County courthouse, ensuring access to legal education for those unable to afford representation. She is also a frequent lecturer at Continuing Legal Education (CLE) programs, where she shares her knowledge with other attorneys.

Francine has held several leadership positions throughout her career, including Chair of the Essex County Bar Association’s Family Law Committee for over 15 years and a seat on the Family Law Executive Committee of the New Jersey State Bar Association. She has also served as a Trustee and past President of the Essex County Bar Association, where she worked closely with judges and attorneys to improve communication and address systemic challenges.

Additionally, she has contributed her time to the New Jersey Supreme Court’s Ethics Committee, serving two terms on District VC (West Essex), and is currently serving her second consecutive four-year term.

Francine’s commitment to the field of family law is unwavering.

Francine earned her Juris Doctorate from Seton Hall University School of Law and holds a bachelor’s degree in psychology from Seton Hall University as well.

She resides in Essex County and is a widow. When Francine is not with her clients, or learning more about interesting legal issues, she is typically baking, cooking, and spending time with her family.

attorneys.name: Joseph J. Asterita
attorneys.practice_type: Real estate Lawyers in Red Bank, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Asterita is a partner at the law firm of Bonfiglio & Asterita, LLC, with offices located in both Red Bank, New Jersey, and Staten Island, New York. He is admitted to practice law in both New Jersey and New York as well as in the United States District Courts for the District of New Jersey and the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York. Mr. Asterita focuses on providing clients with his expertise in three primary practice areas; Real Estate, Estate Planning and Settlement, and Business Law.

Mr. Asterita provides excellent representation to his individual and corporate clients in various real estate matters, including residential and commercial purchases and sales, short sales, refinances and leases. He has successfully handled numerous related real estate litigation matters and disputes ranging from the enforcement of easements and property lines to the partition and sale of residential and commercial properties. Mr. Asterita further supervises the firm’s mortgage loan closing department and represents mortgage lenders in connection with the closing and settlement of mortgage loans, whether in connection with a purchase or refinance, and even reverse mortgages. Mr. Asterita is experienced in closing refinances that incorporate a CEMA designed to help borrowers avoid the costs of the substantial mortgage recording tax in New York, especially involving properties throughout the five boroughs of New York City where the mortgage recording tax is especially high.

Mr. Asterita also provides wealth preservation services through his estate planning expertise, which includes the preparation of wills and trusts and the skillful incorporation of these instruments into comprehensive estate plans. He has written several articles on the subject (available on his firm’s home page www.BonfiglioAsteritaLaw.com) and further provides representation to clients who have an interest in the settlement of an estate, whether by way of probate or administration, as well as handling estate litigation matters involving various disputes including distribution of an estate’s assets, enforcement of a spouse or child’s right to inheritance, enforcing or defending creditor’s claims, or involving the failure of an executor or administrator to properly carry out their fiduciary duties.

As an experienced business attorney, Mr. Asterita serves as a trusted advisor to a wide variety of clients ranging in type from individual entrepreneurs, restaurants and contractors, to public relations, media and information technology firms. He effectively handles their business formation and structuring needs, as well as handling commercial contracts, leases, business purchases and sales, and has handled and resolved numerous shareholder disputes and commercial litigation matters for his diverse clientele.

Mr. Asterita earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in International Affairs at The George Washington University in 1996 and his Juris Doctor degree from Brooklyn Law School in 1999. While attending Brooklyn Law School Mr. Asterita studied abroad at the University of Bologna, Italy, where he focused on Business Law. He is a member of the New Jersey and New York State Bar Associations, the American Bar Association, the Monmouth and Richmond County Bar Associations, the Eastern Monmouth County Chamber of Commerce and the Richmond County Chamber of Commerce.

attorneys.name: Bruce L. Atkins Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Hackensack, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Bruce L. Atkins, Esq. has been practicing law since 1977. He received his undergraduate degree from the University of Connecticut and has a law degree from Seton Hall University School of Law.

He has been admitted to practice in the State Court of New Jersey, the Federal Court of New Jersey, the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, as well as the State of New York, the State of Florida and the U.S. Supreme Court.

He is the senior litigation partner at the law firm of Deutsch Atkins, and his major responsibility is civil litigation with emphasis on employment law. He is highly regarded by his clients for his skills as a NJ employment attorney.

He has had articles published, including Oral employment contracts under New Jersey Law; Are Employees Still Second Class Citizens? Published in the Labor and Employment Law Quarterly in 1994, and Complete Anti-Discrimination Policies the Key, published in Business Insurance, a Crains Publication in October of 1997.

He has also had several major reported cases in the Supreme Court of the State of New Jersey and in the Appellate Division. In addition, he has tried numerous cases in the State and Federal Courts of New Jersey as well as in Federal Court in New York. He obtained a verdict in a sex discrimination case in November of 1996 in the amount of $6.5 Million, $1.5 Million in Compensatory Damages and $5 Million in Punitive Damages. The Court also awarded $638,000 in counsel fees and costs. That verdict was upheld on appeal.

He has been engaged in the practice of law since 1977. In 2006, he merged his practice with the practice of Neil H. Deutsch to form the present firm. In recognition of Mr. Atkins' skill as an employment law attorney in NJ, he is selected for inclusion in the New Jersey Super Lawyers list in 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 in Employment Litigation. A topnotch NJ employment law attorney, he is also AV rated with Martindale-Hubbell since 1997. In 2007, he was selected as a fellow in the Litigation Counsel of America. He has a well-deserved reputation among his peers as a talented New Jersey employment attorney.

He is a member of the American Association for Justice (AAJ), the NJ American Association for Justice, the American Bar Association, the New Jersey Bar Association, the Florida Bar, and the National Employment Lawyers Association (NELA) and NELA NJ. In addition, he has been a guest lecturer at NELA's national convention on trial techniques, at Lorman Seminars and appears regularly as a commentator on Court TV.

If you have been charged with a criminal offense, finding skilled legal help quickly is crucial. Don't take a criminal charge lightly - it may result in substantial fines, incarceration and limited career options. I am attorney Gwendolyn O. Austin. I will represent you aggressively and advise you of your options so you can make informed decisions.

Serious legal problems require immediate intervention. A skilled criminal defense attorney will protect your rights and negotiate for the best possible result. Since 2002, I have represented clients facing criminal charges in Newark and throughout New Jersey. I have earned the trust and confidence of my clients. If you are facing criminal charges or serious traffic citations, I will fight for your rights and provide you with the information necessary to decide how to proceed with your case. Contact me, Newark, New Jersey, criminal defense lawyer Gwendolyn O. Austin, at 866-533-8800 to schedule a free initial consultation.

Dependable, Reliable, Committed

At The Law Office of Gwendolyn O. Austin, you will receive reliable legal help whenever you need it. From routine traffic violations to juvenile offenses to criminal charges, I will use my experience to your benefit and focus my attention on your case. I am committed to providing my clients with quality legal services when it counts the most.

I will work hard to protect your interests and fight for your rights. I will act as a zealous advocate on your behalf.

The phone is answered 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so you can get answers to your questions right away. Whether your matter involves Commercial Driver's License (CDL) repair, traffic violations or other criminal law charges, I am committed to providing you with sound legal advice and professional legal representation.

You can count on me. Contact me at The Law Office of Gwendolyn O. Austin for a free initial consultation.

attorneys.bio:
Founder & Managing Attorney | Law Offices of Peter G. Aziz & Associates LLC

Peter G. Aziz is the founder and managing attorney of the Law Offices of Peter G. Aziz & Associates LLC. A graduate of Widener University School of Law at just 23 years old, Peter distinguished himself early on as one of the youngest graduates in the school’s history — a testament to his ambition, discipline, and passion for the law.

Peter brings extensive trial experience to his practice, having successfully tried hundreds of cases to verdict as lead trial counsel. He has argued and prevailed in both Municipal and State Courts, earning a reputation for his courtroom presence, strategic thinking, and relentless advocacy. Beyond litigation, Peter is also a trusted advisor and transactional attorney, having closed thousands of real estate transactions — from high-value portfolio deals to straightforward residential transfers.

As the managing attorney of the firm, Peter leads with a clear, client-first philosophy: “What would I expect from my attorney if I were the client?” This guiding principle informs not only the quality of legal work but also the responsiveness and integrity that clients experience every day. His leadership ensures that both the firm’s goals and clients’ needs are met with excellence and care.

Peter is currently appointed to the New Jersey Supreme Court Ethics Committee for District VC, where he helps uphold the highest standards of professionalism in the legal community.

Fluent in English and Arabic, Peter brings a global perspective to his practice. Outside the office, he is an avid watch collector, a dedicated martial arts enthusiast, and most importantly, a family man.

attorneys.bio:
Hannah E. Bacon is an Associate Attorney specializing in employment law, child sexual abuse, and sexual assault cases throughout New York and New Jersey. She represents employees in cases involving unlawful workplace discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and wrongful termination, as well as survivors of childhood sexual abuse and adult survivors of sexual assault.

Originally from Morristown, Tennessee, Hannah attended law school in New York City with the aspiration of becoming an attorney who represents survivors of abuse and unlawful discrimination. Hannah is passionate about helping survivors seek accountability from those who have unlawfully violated their rights and is dedicated to advancing the needs and best interests of her clients.

Hannah is currently admitted to practice in New York and New Jersey.

attorneys.name: Marisa Baker
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Violence Trials Lawyers in Flemington, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Marisa Baker Trofimov is a graduate of Yale University and Seton Hall University School of Law, Prior to joining the Law Offices of William P. Deni, Sr. as "Of Counsel", Ms. Trofimov was formerly associated with the law firms Copeland, Shimalla, Wechsler & Lepp and Pellettier, Rabstein & Altman. She has substantial experience handling domestic violence trials, abuse and neglect matters, civil unions, custody and parenting time disputes, palimony cases, and divorce cases, including those of high net worth individuals. Although Ms. Trofimov has trial experience, she is also experienced at resolving matrimonial disputes through mediation, rather than proceeding to trial, which can be cost prohibitive for some clients. She has appeared in Hunterdon, Somerset, Mercer, Warren, Morris, Middlesex, Burlington, Union and Essex County Courts. She is also a former Professor of Family Law at Raritan Valley Community College.

Ms. Trofimov is also experienced at handling estate probate matters.

Prior to entering private practice, Ms. Trofimov was a Law Clerk for the Honorable Heidi Wills Currier, J.S.C., Middlesex County. Prior to attending law school, she served on the legislative staff for Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) handling Health Care, Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security and Women's Issues and was previously a legislative intern for Senator John Kerry (D-MA). She was also paralegal for Sidley, Austin, Brown & Wood in the corporate law department (Pooled Investment Entities) of their New York office prior to attending law school.

Ms. Trofimov is the Hunterdon County Representative to the Young Lawyer's Division of the New Jersey State Bar Association. She is also actively involved in the State Bar Association through the Women In the Profession Section (WHIPS), the Solo and Small Firm Section, and the Family Law Section. Additionally, Ms. Trofimov is an active member of the Hunterdon County Bar Associations and the Somerset County Bar Associations.

attorneys.name: Theodore J. Baker
attorneys.practice_type: New Jersey Division of Child Protection and Permanency (DCPP), formerly known as DYFS Lawyers in Marlton, NJ
attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years, Ted Baker has handled a wide array of complex and sensitive legal matters. Ted has primarily focused on defending families being investigated by the New Jersey Division of Child Protection and Permanency (DCPP), formerly known as DYFS. He has also handled matters regarding adoptions, kinship legal guardianships, criminal defense, and personal injury.

Before opening his law practice, Ted served as Deputy Attorney General representing DCPP. He represented the State in thousands of cases. During that time, he gained valuable experience in matters of child abuse and neglect, termination of parental rights, grandparents, rights, and administrative issues. He brings this insider knowledge and understanding of how DCPP operates when defending his clients.

In addition to his work defending New Jersey families, Ted has also successfully represented clients facing indictable and nonindictable criminal violations. From simple traffic violations and disorderly conduct to assault and homicide charges, Ted has fought for the rights of his clients for over 20 years.

Ted is a Camden County Bar Association member and of the Thomas S. Forkin Inns of Court.

attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Elmwood Park, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Cathy Baleiron, an Immigration Law Associate, has been practicing law for 16 years and joined the Shulman Law Group in 2015. Ms. Baleiron previously worked as the Supervising Immigration Attorney at Northeast New Jersey Legal Services, where she represented individuals before USCIS and the Immigration Court, with a specialization in family-based immigration cases.

She was credited with helping to create the tri-county Immigration Representation Project and was in charge of supervising other immigration attorneys, paralegals, and law students. Her honors include: The 2015 Paterson Alliance Extra Mile Award and the 2007 Legal Services of New Jersey Madeline L. Houston Outstanding Attorney Award. Ms. Baleiron has also conducted numerous Citizenship Clinics, Immigrant Rights workshops, and Immigration training sessions on various immigration topics.

Ms. Baleiron attended New York Law School where she participated in the school’s Immigration Clinic. She holds a Bachelor’s Degree from New York University. Additionally, she studied at the William and Mary School of Law in Madrid, Spain. She is admitted to practice law in New York and New Jersey and is fluent in Spanish.

attorneys.name: Joan M. Bannan
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury and Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Morristown, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Joan Bannan is counsel to Porzio Bromberg & Newman and a member of the Personal Injury and Medical Malpractice Team. She is a trial attorney whose diverse background enables her to be a thoughtful, strategic advocate who effectively evaluates and anticipates factual and legal issues to best represent her clients.

Prior to joining Porzio, Joan's experience included civil litigation, criminal prosecution and professional claims management. Formerly, as a medical malpractice defense attorney, she gained extensive jury trial litigating cases involving catastrophic injuries including neurological brain damage, loss of limbs, loss of vision and death. As an assistant prosecutor in Morris County, she tried felony cases and presented before the Grand Jury as a member of the trial team. During her tenure with a national professional liability insurer, she collaborated with insureds and panel counsel to create and implement innovative strategies to secure favorable resolutions. She also negotiated multi-million dollar settlements and monitored jury trials.

Outside the office, Joan is committed to public service and volunteerism. She was elected as a Bernards Township Committeewoman in 2018 and serves on several municipal boards and commissions. She is a volunteer speaker at community and school events concerning adolescent substance use disorder. Joan is also certified by the National Council for Behavioral Health as a Youth Mental Health First Aid Instructor and has trained over 100 members of her community including local school districts' administrators and teachers.

Joan Bannan has approximately 40 years of experience.

attorneys.name: Sandra M. Barsoum
attorneys.firm_name: Kates Nussman Ellis Earle & Landolfi LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Hackensack, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Sandra M. Barsoum is a Partner of the Firm. She was admitted to practice in New Jersey and New York in 2015, and is also admitted in the District Court of New Jersey and the Southern District of New York.

Ms. Barsoum's practice focuses on civil litigation. She has extensive experience in handling a variety of matters within the realm of employment law, such as New Jersey discrimination claims ("NJLAD"), sexual assault, and hostile-work environment. Ms. Barsoum also represents employers in Wage and Labor disputes and other complex business matters.

Ms. Barsoum's practice involves Estate Administration, which includes but is not limited to, drafting wills and Trust and representing clients in contested estate litigation. Ms. Barsoum is also involved in landlord/tenant practice, which includes representing residential and commercial landlords in summary dispossess proceedings, complex commercial tenancy litigation, residential evictions and commercial lease disputes. Her practice also includes residential real estate transactions.

Ms. Barsoum received her law degree from Michigan State University College of Law where she developed a passion for advocacy. As a law student, Ms. Barsoum interned for the Honorable Judge Curtis Bell in the 9th Circuit Court in Kalamazoo County, Michigan, Family law Division. She was a legal intern at the Legal Services of South Central Michigan in Lansing, Michigan-where she provided legal advice and representation to low-income clients within the realm of family, consumer and housing law.
