attorneys.name: Jose I. Bastarrika Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Woodland Park, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Jose I. Bastarrika is a founding partner of Bastarrika, Soto, Gonzalez & Somohano, LLP founded in 2000. He concentrates his practice in the area of Family Law and is the Managing Partner of the Firm’s Family Law Department.

Mr. Bastarrika served as a Judicial Law Clerk to a Superior Court Judge in the Family Division in Passaic County. He has been a Court Appointed Guardian Ad Litem in complex child custody, child abuse and neglect actions and a Court Appointed Mediator.

A Rule 1:40 Qualified Matrimonial Mediator, Mr. Bastarrika is a panel chair of a Passaic County Matrimonial Early Settlement Panel, and a former Barrister in the Justice Clifford American Inns of Court and the Northern New Jersey Family Law Inns of Court. He has been appointed to the Child Custody and Parenting Committee of the Family Law Section of the New Jersey State Bar Association, the New Jersey State Bar Family Law Executive Committee and appointed by the NJ Supreme Court to serve on the AD HOC Committee on Domestic Violence Reform.

He was selected by the New Jersey Supreme Court to serve as Section Chair of the Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee and is a former member the District XI Fee Arbitration Committee.

A member of the New Jersey State Bar, Passaic County Bar and former Executive Committee member of The Hispanic Bar Associations of New Jersey, Mr. Bastarrika lectures regularly at the New Jersey Institute of Continuing Legal Education on the issue of Professional Responsibility. He has appeared as a Legal Commentator on Court TV and, Telemundo and Univision. Mr. Bastarrika has been selected as a Super Lawyer by the New Jersey Monthly Magazine.

Jose is fluent in Spanish and a proud graduate of Rutgers College in New Brunswick and Rutgers School of Law.

attorneys.name: R. Daniel Bausé
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Springfield, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Dan Bause has been associate at O’Connor, Parsons, Lane & Noble LLC since 2012 and has amassed extensive litigation and trial experience in that time. Dan specializes in employment law, with a significant emphasis in wrongful termination and workplace harassment matters. Particularly, Dan has represented numerous employees in cases against their current and former employers in a variety of different claims, including sexual and racial harassment, hostile work environment, race discrimination, disability discrimination, age discrimination, pregnancy discrimination, unlawful retaliation and violations of the FMLA and NJFLA. Many of these cases have resulted in substantial recoveries and settlements for the firm’s clients and Dan continues to fight for employees’ rights within the workplace in a number of different capacities. Dan also handles personal injury matters for the firm, including slip and falls, car accidents and other similar matters and also has trial experience relating to such claims.

Dan received his B.S. magna cum laude from Seton Hall University in 2008 and his J.D. magna cum laude from Seton Hall University School of Law in 2011. He is a member of Seton Hall Law’s chapter of the Order of the Coif and received the Chicago Title Insurance Company Award upon graduation. While at Seton Hall Law, Dan served as an Associate Editor for the SHU Law Sports and Entertainment Law Journal and as a clinical student in the SHU Law’s Civil Rights and Constitutional Litigation Clinic. It was during his time as a clinical student fighting for the civil rights of various clients where Dan developed a passion for civil rights and ultimately led him to the litigation of such claims within the workplace.

Prior to joining the firm, Dan served as the law clerk for the Honorable Martin Cronin, J.S.C. in the Superior Court of New Jersey – Essex County. Dan is admitted to practice law in both New Jersey and New York and is a member of such organizations as the New Jersey Bar Association and the National Employment Lawyers Association.

attorneys.bio:
Andrew J. Bayne, Esq. had dedicated his professional career to the representation of sophisticated global businesses based both abroad and in the United States. Andrew received his B.A. degree from Rutgers University and his J.D. degree from the Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law. attorneys.name: Thomas J. Bean
attorneys.firm_name: Weinberger Divorce & Family Law Group, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family and Matrimonial Law Lawyers in Freehold, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Thomas J. Bean, Esq. is a family law attorney at Weinberger Divorce & Family Law Group, LLC. Mr. Bean is an experienced and highly accomplished legal advocate who has handled countless family and matrimonial matters in his career, including divorce, child custody, child support, domestic violence, adoption, post-judgment modifications, enforcement of family court orders, and other related family law matters.

Mr. Bean’s choice to focus his practice exclusively on family law comes from his deep affinity for guiding individuals through difficult family law issues with sound legal advice and compassionate communication. Drawing upon over a decade of experience in family law, Mr. Bean understands how to skillfully select the optimal strategy and legal arguments for his clients’ family law matters, including sensitive child custody issues. Mr. Bean is committed to delivering zealous representation and strives to achieve the best possible results for his clients, whether through litigation or settlement.

Mr. Bean previously worked in a variety of areas including municipal law, criminal law, bankruptcy law, real estate law, estate planning and administration, civil litigation, and family litigation. This broad background has provided Mr. Bean with crucial knowledge of other areas of law which often intersect with family practice, enabling Mr. Bean to provide more comprehensive counsel to his clients when issues relating to these areas of law arise during the divorce process.

Mr. Bean is a graduate of Seton Hall University School of Law. During his time in law school, he interned with two New Jersey Superior Court judges as well as prosecutor’s offices in New Jersey and New York. Mr. Bean began his career as a judicial law clerk to Hon. Ronald L. Reisner, J.S.C. in the Superior Court of New Jersey, Criminal Division, Monmouth Vicinage. Mr. Bean’s time as an intern and as a judicial law clerk allowed him to develop a close familiarity with the operations of the court system and deepened his understanding of New Jersey law and its application to cases and issues before the court.

Prior to attending law school, Mr. Bean graduated from Villanova University. While in college, Mr. Bean participated in internships with a tax law and economic advisory firm in London, UK and with the United Nations Environment Program in Geneva, Switzerland, while also completing coursework at the London School of Economics. Mr. Bean’s educational background assists him in analyzing the financial aspects of divorce, including the calculation of support obligations and the valuation of business interests, in order to secure positive economic outcomes for his clients.

Mr. Bean has a longstanding connection to Monmouth County, having attended Christian Brothers Academy for high school and having spent several years working as an intern and law clerk in the Monmouth County Courthouse as well as for other law firms in the area.

Mr. Bean is admitted to the Bar of the State of New Jersey and the District Court of New Jersey. Mr. Bean volunteers as an Early Settlement Panelist in Middlesex County. Mr. Bean has also participated in the Aldona E. Appleton Family Law Inn of Court and is a member of the New Jersey State Bar Association and the Middlesex County Bar Association.

Mr. Bean resides in Mercer County with his wife, their two daughters, and their black lab.

attorneys.name: Jessica Beardsley
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Marlton, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Jessica attended college with the intention of becoming a marriage and family counselor. As she attended various classes, including some prelaw classes, she decided to attend law school so she could take a more active role in helping people when they are at their most vulnerable.

During law school, she volunteered with the Domestic Violence Project and joined the Domestic Violence Clinic. After graduation, she was awarded the Lisa and Kolin Pimental Award for Excellence in the Study of Domestic Violence Law. She was also awarded the Mary Philbrook award in September 2018.

After law school, she clerked for the Hon. David Ragonese in the Camden County Superior Court. Even though she clerked in the Criminal Division, she knew that she wanted to continue her focus on family law in the next phase of her career.

Jessica has been practicing as an associate attorney in family law since September 2019 and has focused on developing connections with her clients to help them through what may be the most emotional time in their life.

She is a member and active participant in the Burlington County and Camden County Bar Associations and she serves clients in Atlantic County, Burlington County, Camden County, Cumberland County, Gloucester County, Mercer County, Monmouth County, and Salem County.

attorneys.bio:
Gregory D. R. Behringer Esq., joined Laufer, Dalena, Jensen & Doran, LLC in September 2011 following a judicial clerkship with the Honorable James M. DeMarzo, Superior Court Judge for the Family Division, Morris County, New Jersey.

Mr. Behringer received his Bachelor of Science in Chemistry and Economics from Hampden-Sydney College and his Juris Doctorate from Ohio Northern University “With Distinction” where he was an Associate Justice of Moot Court. During his law school tenure, he interned at the Rose Immigration Law Firm in Nashville, Tennessee, and completed an externship with Judge Walter H. Rice, United States District Court, Southern District of Ohio. Also, while in law school Mr. Behringer passed the Patent Agent Exam and was admitted to practice Patent Law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (“USPTO”).

Mr. Behringer is an accomplished oral advocate and was the Champion of the Anthony J. Celebrezze Appellate Advocacy Competition where he placed first among all law students in intra-school appellate advocacy competition. Additionally, he was the Champion of the Dan Guy Appellate Advocacy Program where he placed first among his class of over 100 fellow students.

Following law school, he completed a clerkship with the Honorable James M. DeMarzo, Family Part, Morris County prior to joining the firm. Mr. Behringer is a member of the New Jersey State Bar Association, the Morris County Bar Association, and the Barry Croland Family Law Inn of Court.

Mr. Behringer presently serves as the Vice Chair of the District X Ethics Fee Arbitration Committee. He has served on the Morris County Early Settlement Panel since 2014. He has presented numerous continuing legal education seminars on family related matters both for the Morris County Bar Association and the New Jersey Institute of Continuing Legal Education. He has also published articles in the Matrimonial Strategists.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Laurie A Bernstein, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce and Family Law Lawyers in Roseland, NJ
attorneys.bio:
With so many family law firms to choose from, why select my firm to handle your divorce, custody and parenting time, child support, alimony and cohabitation issues, post-judgement disputes, domestic violence and other family law matters.

The answer is simple - I have been a family law practitioner for over 40 years licensed in three states. I have the experience, dedication, passion and knowledge to work hand in hand with you to help you to reach your goals. I care about my clients and want to achieve the best results for them. I listen to you and hear you. We work together as a team from the inception of your case to create creative and common sense solutions to those simple to complex issues. If amicable resolutions cannot be reached, I will aggressively try your case. Having previously worked in other areas of the law throughout my career along with family law, such a personal injury, workers compensation, and government benefits, my experience in those areas enhances my knowledge in handling your divorce/family law case. For more than a decade, I served as a Blue Ribbon Mandatory Early Settlement Panelist, Chairperson of the District VC Fee Arbitration Committee and lecturer in the community regarding relevant and emerging family law topics.

What also distinguishes my firm, is that you get me - an experienced attorney from start to finish. I know you and I know your case. I am there for you. I do not spend my time and your money educating paralegals or junior associates about you and your case and only show up for "major events." Every event in your case is important to you and important to me in building the case towards attaining your ultimate result.

I have a long-term successful practice, satisfied clients who return time and again even after many years, and refer me to their family and closest friends.

If amicable resolutions cannot be reached, I will aggressively try your case. Having previously worked in other areas of the law throughout my career along with family law, such a personal injury, workers compensation, and government benefits, my experience in those areas enhances my knowledge in handling your divorce/family law case. For more than a decade, I served as a Blue Ribbon Mandatory Early Settlement Panelist, Chairperson of the District VC Fee Arbitration Committee and lecturer in the community regarding relevant and emerging family law topics.

What also distinguishes my firm, is that you get me - an experienced attorney from start to finish. I know you and I know your case. I am there for you. I do not spend my time and your money educating paralegals or junior associates about you and your case and only show up for "major events." Every event in your case is important to you and important to me in building the case towards attaining your ultimate result.

I have a long-term successful practice, satisfied clients who return time and again even after many years, and refer me to their family and closest friends.

attorneys.name: Daniel R. Bevere
attorneys.firm_name: Piro Zinna Cifelli Paris & Genitempo LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Nutley, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Daniel R. Bevere, a partner at Piro Zinna Cifelli Paris & Genitempo, is a seasoned trial attorney with substantial jury trial experience. His practice is among the most diverse of any attorney in the litigation department, having successfully tried to conclusion many cases in the areas of personal injury and medical malpractice, insurance defense, first party insurance coverage claims and subrogation matters, civil rights and construction litigation, business disputes, foreclosures, lender liability, estate and trust litigation, commercial landlord-tenant matters and criminal defense. Dan also has extensive appellate experience, having argued numerous times before the appeals courts of the State of New Jersey, including the N.J. Supreme Court, as well as the United States Third Circuit Court of Appeals.

He has been a public defender for the Borough of Kenilworth, New Jersey since 1995 and counsel to the Essex Regional Health Commission, prosecuting violations of the State and Regional Air Pollution Control Codes. Dan has been a member of the Bar of the State of New Jersey since 1994. He is currently a member of the Essex County Bar Association, the American Trial Lawyer's Association and the New Jersey Association for Justice.

Prior to joining the firm in 1995, he was an attorney with McCarter & English, where he practiced in the areas of commercial litigation, lender liability, foreclosures and bankruptcy and developed an expertise in the specialized area of asset recovery. He also co-authored an article on lender liability defenses which was published in the New Jersey Law Journal. Dan graduated cum laude in 1991 from Boston College in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts and graduated magna cum laude in 1994 from Seton Hall School of Law.

Rajat is a trial attorney in the North Jersey team for Garces, Grabler & LeBrocq. His areas of practice focus on personal injury litigation, including catastrophic injuries. Rajat has experience litigating across New Jersey state and federal courts. He has also successfully represented clients in various appeals to the Appellate Division and Supreme Court of New Jersey.

Rajat’s stamina for relentless advocacy and meticulous preparation of each case for trial make him a formidable litigator. Rajat prides himself in his relationships with his clients, with whom he maintains constant communication. Treating each client like family. Rajat has secured numerous six figure and seven figure settlements for personal injury cases, including motor vehicle accidents, slip and fall, and product liability matters.

Prior to joining GGL, Rajat was a managing attorney at a mid-size litigation firm in Paramus, New Jersey. He began his legal career serving as a judicial law clerk to the Hon. Margaret Goodzeit, P.J.Ch. for Somerset, Warren, and Hunterdon counties.

In law school, Rajat represented small businesses in commercial litigation actions against large multinational corporations at the legal clinic. He also participated in five trial and appellate moot court competitions, with high ranks nationally and regionally. From the inception of his legal career, Rajat knew that he wanted to be an advocate for those who needed a voice.

In his free time, Rajat enjoys the sport of boxing, Muay Thai, and golf.

attorneys.name: Paul M. Bishop
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Princeton, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Paul M. Bishop is a Director with the firm. Paul’s practice focuses on business, commercial, and general litigation. Throughout his career, Paul has represented clients in a variety of complex disputes in federal and state court involving contracts, commercial issues, fraud, insurance law, corporate law, constitutional issues, bankruptcy, employment discrimination, copyright/trademark infringement, and personal injury. Paul’s wide-ranging experience allows him to handle a variety of litigation matters with ease and skill.

Paul is known for managing legal matters efficiently and economically from inception to conclusion of trial and through any subsequent appeal process. He is particularly adept at all facets of the litigation process, discovery, motion practice, trial preparation, trial and appeal.

Recent Litigation Success

• Negotiated a multi-million dollar shareholder buyout on the eve of trial;

• Won a multi-day trial and obtain an award of treble damages and attorneys’ fees for a homeowner victimized by a contractor

• Obtained a $500,000 settlement on behalf of a neurosurgical and orthopaedic medical practice in litigation and injunction proceedings against two former employees for breach of restrictive covenant, unfair competition, and violation of New Jersey’s computer offense law

• Obtained a $3 million judgment on behalf of a medical practice declaring it the beneficiary of a life insurance policy and defended this declaratory judgment through subsequent appeal to both the Appellate Division and Supreme Court. IVF Inv. Co. LLC v. Estate of Natofsky, 2012 WL 1813429 (N.J. Super Ct. App. Div. May 21, 2012)

• Successfully argued a motion to dismiss a claim for disability discrimination against New Jersey orthopedic practice. Leone v. N. Jersey Orthopaedic Specialists, P.A., 2012 WL 1535198 (D.N.J. Apr. 27, 2012)

• Defeated class certification in a class action seeking to hold a small, New Jersey business liable for allegedly sending a “blast” fax in violation of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. Damages awarded against client were reduced from over $10 million to $650

• Obtained summary judgment on behalf of corporation alleged to have committed numerous violations of the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination

• Successfully defended a doctor from multi-million-dollar allegations of assault from a former patient, obtaining a “no-cause” verdict after several days of trial

• Successfully prosecuted a separate defamation claim against the same former patient on behalf of the doctor resulting in an award in favor of the client after several days of trial

• Successfully negotiated a mediated, six-figure settlement award on behalf of clients who learned that the newly purchased million-dollar condominium suffered from significant, undisclosed water leaks infiltrations through the home’s windows.

• Obtained summary judgment on behalf of a New Jersey real estate developer requiring return of a six-figure purchase deposit after discovery of asbestos on the subject property. Subsequent to dispute, Defendant remediated the asbestos situation and refused to return the deposit. Paul, through rigorous public record review, discovered the remediation and obtained summary judgment and an award of attorneys’ fees

• After a multi-day trial, obtained a six-figure judgment, punitive damages, and attorneys’ fees against client’s former employee for fraud and conversion

• Discovered a six-figure theft by an attorney representing an estate where his clients were beneficiaries. Obtained return of the 100% of the stolen funds without the need for significant discovery, motion practice or trial.

• Successfully negotiated numerous shareholder disputes without the need for trial or significant litigation

attorneys.name: Daniel J. Bitonti
attorneys.practice_type: Business law Lawyers in Edison, NJ
attorneys.bio:
In 2019, my world was turned upside down when my father, a respected attorney in New Jersey for nearly 40 years, passed away unexpectedly after a brief illness. He was a man who dedicated his life to helping others, practicing personal injury law with a commitment to ensuring that those who were injured received the justice they deserved. He was nearing retirement but still had active cases, loyal clients, and a reputation built on trust and diligence. People relied on him, and they knew he would fight for them.

But when he passed, there was no succession plan for his practice. His filing system was a relic of another era, and he had very little support staff to carry on the work he had meticulously handled himself. His clients, many of whom were in the midst of their own battles, were left in a state of uncertainty. They were scared, confused, and anxious about what would happen to their cases, their lives hanging in the balance.

Usually, in situations like this, where an attorney dies without appointing a trustee to manage the affairs of their firm, the court steps in, appointing someone to sort through the chaos. But I couldn’t let that happen—not to my father’s legacy, not to the clients who had put their trust in him. Despite having my own professional responsibilities, I knew I had to step into his shoes, to ensure that nothing fell through the cracks.

It was an immense responsibility. I had no prior experience in personal injury law, so I had to learn quickly—studying this particular area of law, deciphering his antiquated filing system, and navigating the complexities of running a law firm. There were moments of frustration where I questioned whether I could really do this, whether I could honor my father’s legacy while still managing my own life.

But I wasn’t alone. My father had built strong professional relationships over the years, and one of his close colleagues, a seasoned personal injury attorney, became my mentor. He guided me through some of the toughest challenges, offering advice and reassurance when I needed it most. Together, we worked to ensure that the clients received the attention and care they deserved, that their cases were properly handled, and that funds in the trust account were disbursed correctly.

It was a journey filled with highs and lows. There were days when the stress was overwhelming, when the sheer volume of work seemed insurmountable. But there were also moments of deep satisfaction, knowing that I was making a difference—not just for my father’s clients, but for my mother, who did not have to worry about hiring someone to manage the firm’s affairs. Over the course of 18 months, I was able to bring order to the chaos, to provide the stability that everyone involved so desperately needed.

This experience, while challenging, was also incredibly rewarding. It taught me the value of perseverance, of stepping up when it matters most. And it gave me a deep empathy for those who find themselves in situations where they don’t know where to turn, who feel overwhelmed by the complexities of their circumstances. I know what it’s like to face uncertainty, to carry the burden of responsibility, and to find a way through to the other side.

And that’s why I’m here—to help others navigate their own legal challenges, to provide the guidance and support they need to achieve the best possible outcome. Because I’ve been there, I’ve lived it, and I understand the emotions that come with it.

I help business owners fund, grow, protect, and sell their businesses. I focus on solving problems related to raising capital, contracts, business disputes, and acquisitions. I learned how to win a fight by litigating in state and federal courts, in front of New Jersey administrative bodies and land use boards. My extensive experience, spanning over 20 years in law firms, has honed my skills in helping everyday people with business challenges.

As the son of an attorney, I developed a deep understanding and passion for the law from an early age. I graduated from Rutgers Law School and now proudly serve clients in the Garden State. In my personal life, I’m devoted to my family - my wife, two daughters and son. I apply the same dedication to the clients I represent.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Jeffrey M. Bloom
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in West New York, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey M. Bloom was born in New York, NY. He moved to New Jersey as a young child and has lived in northern New Jersey for over forty (40) years.

Mr. Bloom received his Undergraduate Degree in Business Administration from Emory University in 1985. Thereafter, he obtained his Juris Doctorate from Brooklyn Law School in 1988 where he served as a member of the Editorial Board of the Brooklyn Journal of International Law.

Mr. Bloom is licensed to practice law in New Jersey, New York, and the District of Columbia as well as the Supreme Court of the United States of America and various other federal courts.

Jeffrey Bloom is a second generation attorney. His father, Irwin Bloom, graduated New York University Law School and practiced in New York City for over forty (40) years, primarily representing defendants and insurance companies. As a young man, Jeffrey Bloom realized that he did not want to represent corporations, but that he wanted to dedicate his career to defending the rights of individuals, including people crippled in horrible accidents or families torn apart by divorce. For more than the past twenty (20) years of his career, Mr. Bloom has worked hard to build a reputation as an attorney who will fight for the rights of his clients whether battling a manipulative spouse or an unsympathetic corporation.

Mr. Bloom is an active member of the American and New Jersey's Trial Lawyer's Association where he is a contributing member of both the Personal Injury and Family Law Listserves. He is also a member of the New Jersey, Hudson and Bergen County Bar Associations. AV rated* under Martindale-Hubbell's peer review rating system, he is a member of the Association of Trial Lawyers of New Jersey and the Family Law Listserv. He has also appeared on local and national TV - if your case generates media attention, he has the experience to speak for you. Mr. Bloom has also been designated a SuperLawyer.

attorneys.name: Kristen Blucher Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Livingston, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Kristen Blucher is an Associate Attorney with Ziegler Law Group LLC since July 2023. Kristen is licensed to practice law in the State of New Jersey. She is a seasoned practitioner in the area of family law, with experience handling a wide range of matters through litigation and collaborative processes.

Practice Areas

Kristen has extensive experience representing clients in complex and emotionally charged family law matters, including:

Divorce, including high-conflict divorce matters;

Child custody and parenting time disputes;

Prenuptial agreements;

High net-worth marital estates;

Pre- and post-judgment motion practice;

Grandparent custody;

Adoption;

Domestic violence matters;

Contested Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act (UCCJEA) matters; and

Appeals in both the Appellate Division and Supreme Court of New Jersey.

Appellate and Complex Litigation Experience

In her appellate practice, Kristen has represented clients in both family and criminal matters on issues including cohabitation, child custody, criminal convictions, and domestic violence. She recently co-authored a brief on behalf of the Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers of New Jersey as amicus curiae in M.A. v. J.H.M., 260 N.J. 522 (2025), in which the Supreme Court of New Jersey ruled that a court may not draw an adverse inference against a defendant in a civil domestic violence trial who invokes the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.

Judicial Clerkship Experience

Kristen served as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable John P. McDonald, J.S.C., Family Part, Somerset County, during the 2020–2021 term. In this role, she assisted the court by researching legal issues, preparing motion orders, and managing divorce, non-dissolution, and domestic violence trials and other proceedings. This experience provided Kristen with valuable insight into judicial decision-making and substantive family law.

Education and Early Legal Experience

Kristen received her Juris Doctor from Boston University School of Law in 2020. While in law school, she gained significant experience as a student attorney serving low-income clients in the greater Boston area through positions in legal clinics at Boston University and Harvard Law School. Kristen also served as staff editor and articles editor on the American Journal of Law & Medicine.

Kristen earned her Bachelor of Arts, summa cum laude, in English from Rutgers University in 2015.

Client-Centered Approach

Kristen understands that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to family law. Her background in legal aid and client-centered lawyering makes her particularly adept at guiding clients through emotionally taxing times. She approaches every matter with empathy, attention to detail, and a strong commitment to achieving her clients’ objectives.

Outside the Office

When not practicing law, Kristen is an avid reader and enjoys spending time with her family and two dogs.

attorneys.name: Stephen J. Bodnar Esquire
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Mount Holly, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Stephen J. Bodnar is a skilled and compassionate criminal defense attorney with more than twenty-five (25) years' experience practicing criminal law. Prior to joining Rosenberg | Perry & Associates, he practiced criminal law as a Burlington County Assistant Prosecutor, where he was responsible for handling thousands of cases at all stages of the criminal justice process, from pre-indictment through appeal.

Mr. Bodnar's vast experience, working in the Grand Jury, Trial, and the Motions and Appeals Units, has provided him with extensive knowledge of all phases of criminal practice and procedure. His experience includes trying homicide, felony murder, sexual assault, robbery, burglary, theft, drug distribution, and all manner of weapons offense cases. For criminal issues on appeal, Mr. Bodnar has appeared and argued numerous times before the Superior Court, Appellate Division.

As a County Prosecutor, Mr. Bodnar oversaw the Burlington County Prosecutor's Office involvement in the New Jersey Superior Court Drug Court Program which has the mission of assisting those with alcohol and drug dependencies to resolve related criminal charges.

Mr. Bodnar has comprehensive and authoritative knowledge in New Jersey's recent Criminal Justice Reform. In 2017, New Jersey's criminal justice system transitioned from a bail program to a system of non-monetary pre-trial release. As the Supervisor of the Grand Jury and Screening Unit in the Burlington County Prosecutor's Office, Mr. Bodnar helped develop and implement the county's pre-trial detention policy and procedures.

As a certified instructor, Mr. Bodnar taught at the Burlington County Police Academy on search and seizure law, Miranda issues, and the New Jersey Criminal Code. He also provided instruction and training to seasoned police officers through the Burlington County Law Enforcement Training Center. Upon the implementation of Criminal Justice Reform/Bail Reform in in 2017, Mr. Bodnar conducted training to all the law enforcement agencies in Burlington County. Mr. Bodnar has been a presenter and panelist at Continuing Legal Education Courses addressing issues regarding criminal justice and bail reform to defense and prosecuting attorneys.

Outside of the legal practice, Mr. Bodnar is an avid follower of minor and major league baseball. He also trains for and participates in ultrarunning events. He has run numerous ultra distance races, including ten 100 mile finishers.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Bonfiglio Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Red Bank, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Before his retirement from the practice of law in 2021, Thomas J. Bonfiglio was a Certified Public Accountant and Attorney with over 30 years' experience. He earned a Bachelor of Business Administration degree from Pace University in 1982 and his Juris Doctor degree from Brooklyn Law School in 1987 and was admitted to practice in the state courts of New York and New Jersey, as well as in the United States Tax Court, and the United States District Courts for the Eastern District of New York and the District of New Jersey. He and Joseph J. Asterita, Esq., were partners in the law firm known as Bonfiglio & Asterita, LLC for nearly 20 years before his retirement in 2021. Tragically, Tom passed away at the age of 62 in 2022, 1 year to the day after he retired from practice. The law firm continues today as Asterita & Associates, LLC – Attorneys at Law.

Mr. Bonfiglio established his accounting firm and law practice in 1989, after gaining substantial legal experience as a tax attorney for the "big 6" accounting firm Arthur Anderson & Co., and as tax counsel to Sony USA. Until his retirement Mr. Bonfiglio counseled a broad range of clients on an array of legal and tax matters, including estate and business succession planning, business structing and represented clients before Federal and State tax authorities as well as the United States Tax Court. He provided counsel and representation to a wide variety of business clients in corporate and commercial transactions and served the needs of his clients on a full range of real property transactions including private and commercial real estate purchases, sales, financing and leases as well as managing the firm’s mortgage loan closing department by representing mortgage lenders in various loan transactions. Mr. Bonfiglio's knowledge and experience served our clients well when they needed not just a lawyer, but also a trusted advisor to provide comprehensive solutions to complex legal problems.

attorneys.name: Kourtney A. Borchers
attorneys.firm_name: Weinberger Divorce & Family Law Group, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mount Laurel, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Kourtney Borchers, Esquire, is an associate attorney at Weinberger Divorce & Family Law Group, LLC. Ms. Borchers received her Juris Doctorate from Pennsylvania State University, Dickinson Law, in 1996. After graduation, in addition to immediately becoming a full-time mother, she became a full-time lawyer where she has spent the last twenty years devoted to representing family law clients by crafting creative legal strategies and providing personalized client service.

Originally from the mid-west, Ms. Borchers moved to New Jersey after graduating from Pennsylvania State University’s Dickinson Law in 1996. Her career began at Quinlan, Dunne, & Daily where she specialized in family law. Since then Ms. Borchers has unwaveringly advocated for individuals faced with the often overwhelming legal process that they face during some of the most difficult times of their lives. She then went on to work as an associate attorney at Davis & Mendelson handling various trial level and appellate level family law matters.

Most recently she worked as the senior associate at Rebel Brown Law Group, handling complex family law matters at both the pre-trial, trial and appellate level.

Ms. Borchers is admitted to the New Jersey Bar and the New Jersey District Court Bar. Ms. Borchers’ practice has been and remains almost exclusively concentrated in matrimonial and family law, where she remains dedicated to serving the best interests of her clients in all matters related to child custody, divorce, support, alimony, and division of assets.

She also volunteers as an expert panelist at the family courts in the Early Settlement Programs. Not only has Ms. BOrchers been a Barrister of the Thomas S. Forkin Family Law Inns of Court, she is presently a member of the New Jersey State Bar Assocation, the Gloucester County Bar Association and the Camden County Bar Association.

Ms. Borchers resides in South Jersey where she is an active member of her community and enjoys spending time with her three daughters.

attorneys.name: Pamela Lynn Brause
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce and Family Lawyers in Metuchen, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Pamela Lynn Brause is a partner at the firm, and has been practicing since 1982.

She has been admitted to the New Jersey State Bar since 1982, the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey since 1982, the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court since 1992.

Ms. Brause graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree from Rutgers College in 1979, and a Juris Doctor from Rutgers Law School in 1982.

She is a member of the Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers of New Jersey, the New Jersey State Bar Association, and the Middlesex County Bar Association.

She serves as a Middlesex County Matrimonial Early Settlement Panelist, and as a 2014-2015 Middlesex County Bar Foundation Trustee. She has also served on the Middlesex County Assignment Judge's Criminal Lawyers Committee and as co-chair of the Middlesex County Bar Association Criminal Committee.

She has lectured on criminal trial practice and attorney ethics, has appeared as a guest commentator on Court TV She has also been interviewed on ABC, NBC, and CBS News on cases in the news, such as the "Sayreville Seven," in which she represented one of the Sayreville High School football players accused of hazing.

She has considerable litigation experience throughout the Courts of New Jersey, having tried more than 100 cases, including capital murder trials, civil lawsuits and workers' compensation, and divorce and custody hearings.

She provides personal attention with effective representation to her clients and their children.

Ms. Brick previously volunteered with Partners for Women and Justice, Montclair, N.J., and the Battered Women’s Legal Advocacy Project (BWLAP), Morris County, N.J. She is licensed to practice before New Jersey State Courts, United States District Court of New Jersey and Supreme Court of New York. She has now been court qualified as a New Jersey Family Law Mediator along with being named a member of the State's Ethics Committee.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Joanna D. Brick is the founder of the firm. She is an admitted state attorney and court qualified mediator with a focus on matrimonial law. For more than 30 years she has worked in the legal field from interning to being a paralegal at some of the most prestigious New Jersey and New York Firms and also with New York City’s Administration of Children’s Services (ACS) where she prosecuted abuse and neglect cases.

After receiving her J.D. from New York Law School, Ms. Brick clerked for Hon. David J. Issenman, Superior Court of N.J., Ch. Div., Family Part – Union County, ret. Since clerking, Ms. Brick has worked at various known law firms until opening her own boutique practice. She provides personal attention with effective representation to her clients and their children.

Ms. Brick previously volunteered with Partners for Women and Justice, Montclair, N.J., and the Battered Women’s Legal Advocacy Project (BWLAP), Morris County, N.J. She is licensed to practice before New Jersey State Courts, United States District Court of New Jersey and Supreme Court of New York. She has now been court qualified as a New Jersey Family Law Mediator along with being named a member of the State's Ethics Committee.

attorneys.name: Sarah Briguglio
attorneys.practice_type: Complex estate planning Lawyers in River Edge, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Sarah is licensed to practice law in New Jersey, New York, Florida and Texas. She is an active member of the New Jersey, New York, Florida and Texas Bar Associations. Sarah focuses her practice on complex estate planning, Medicaid planning, Special Needs planning, guardianships and elder law, trust and estate administration, intergenerational wealth transfer and tax planning and providing business and transactional counsel to clients.

Prior to serving as the lead attorney at Law Offices of Sarah Briguglio, LLC, Sarah practiced in the Trusts & Estates Department at several law firms and served as a law clerk in Superior Court. Sarah utilizes her knowledge of the law in multiple states to assist clients with interstate planning needs. Sarah has conducted various Trial Court sand Surrogate’s Court proceedings throughout the Tristate area and Florida, representing clients in a wide range of practice areas. Sarah draws on her experience counselling clients on a wide array of estate planning and transactional matters to avoid common missteps that may otherwise lead to costly litigation. Sarah further strives to guide her clients on asset protection and wealth transfer to preserve her clients’ estates for future generations. Sarah has also been instrumental in advising and representing clients on succession planning, sale/purchase of their business, shareholder agreements, operating agreements, and buy/sell agreements.

Sarah earned her undergraduate degree from The College of New Jersey where she majored in Psychology and graduated with honors. Sarah went on to pursue her law degree from Seton Hall Law School. During law school, Sarah interned at the US Attorney’s Office, the Attorney General’s Office of New Jersey and with the District Court of New Jersey and served in a pro bono clinic assisting with a death penalty case.

When not practicing law, Sarah enjoys cycling, nature walks, touring art museums and attending the theater.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in New Brunswick, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Victor Broccoli is a workers’ compensation attorney with Garces, Grabler & LeBrocq. Victor is proud to focus his practice exclusively on the rights of injured workers. He has regularly appeared throughout workers’ compensation courts in New Jersey, routinely taking matters to trial and delivering the best possible outcomes for his clients. His passion is for making sure that people injured on the job get the medical treatment and compensation they deserve. He has a track record of securing the best possible outcomes for his clients by being diligent, thorough, and responsive.

Prior to joining Garces, Grabler & LeBrocq, Victor managed the workers’ compensation department for a general litigation firm. Before focusing his practice on representing injured workers in New Jersey, Victor maintained a general law practice in rural North Carolina.

attorneys.name: Nathan L. Broffman
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Red Bank, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Broffman is an associate at McOmber McOmber & Luber, P.C. in the firm’s Marlton, New Jersey office. Mr. Broffman primarily focuses his practice on employment law and civil litigation, representing clients in matters involving discrimination, sexual harassment,retaliation, wrongful termination, and whistleblower claims.

Mr. Broffman graduated from William & Mary in 2019 with a Bachelor of Arts in International Relations. In 2025, Mr. Broffman graduated cum laude from Rutgers Law School – Camden.

During law school, Mr. Broffman received a first-year writing award for his outstanding performance in the Legal Analysis, Writing, and Research I and II courses. Mr. Broffman also served as a legal writing fellow, helping first-year students develop their legal writing and research skills.

After his first year of law school, Mr. Broffman gained invaluable experience as a judicial intern to the Honorable Steven J. Polansky, Presiding Judge of the Civil Division in Camden County, New Jersey. Mr. Broffman conducted legal research, drafted memoranda, and observed proceedings in various civil matters. Following his second year, Mr. Broffman joined the team at McOmber McOmber & Luber, P.C. as a law clerk in the firm’s Marlton office.

Mr. Broffman currently resides in Mount Laurel, New Jersey. In his free time, he enjoys making music and watching his favorite baseball team, the Baltimore Orioles.

attorneys.name: Abbott S. Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Freehold, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Abbott S. Brown is a partner with Lomurro Law in Freehold, New Jersey, where he concentrates on civil litigation with an emphasis in medical and legal malpractice litigation.

Mr. Brown attended Rutgers College in New Brunswick and received his J.D. in 1978 from Rutgers University School of Law, Newark. He is admitted to practice in New Jersey and before the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York, and the Second and Third Circuit Courts of Appeal. Mr. Brown was certified by the New Jersey Supreme Court as a Certified Civil Trial Attorney in 1994, 2001, 2006 and 2013. Mr. Brown is the co-author of New Jersey Legal Malpractice and Litigation Ethics (JAG Press 2021) New Jersey Medical Malpractice Law, (11th Ed., New Jersey Law Journal Books, Newark, N.J., 2021) and New Jersey Medical Malpractice Cases, (3d Ed., Institute for Continuing Legal Education, New Brunswick, N.J. 2009). Mr. Brown is also the author of a chapter titled "Medical Experts," found in New Jersey Trial and Evidence Law (NJICLE 2003). Mr. Brown has had editorials published in the New Jersey Star Ledger, The New York Times and the New Jersey Law Journal. Mr. Brown has also authored over 50 articles for numerous professional publications, and has delivered more than 100 lectures for NJICLE, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America, the New Jersey Association for Justice and other organizations.

Mr. Brown served on the Supreme Court Committee on Model Civil Jury Charges, the Supreme Court Committee on Jury Selection and Voir Dire, and the Board of Governors of the Association of Trial Lawyers of America - New Jersey. He was awarded the Gold Medal for Distinguished Service by the Association of Trial Lawyers of America - New Jersey in April of 2001. Mr. Brown was recognized as one of the 50 Most Powerful People in New Jersey Healthcare in 2012.

Mr. Brown was an Adjunct Professor at Seton Hall University School of Law in the Health Law and Policy Program, where he taught medical malpractice law from 1998 to 2010. He also lectured at the New Jersey Judicial College and served on the Board of Trustees of the Trial Attorneys of New Jersey and the District V-B Ethics Committee, and as Chair of the Medical Malpractice Committee of the New Jersey State Bar Association. Mr. Brown has also served as a delegate to the New Jersey State Bar Association - Third Annual Judicial Administration Forum, and on the Special Committee on Implementation of a Pilot Medical Malpractice Mediation project.

attorneys.name: Randall H. Brown Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mount Laurel, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Randall graduated from Syracuse University with a degree in Political Science and a minor in Political Philosophy. He went on to earn his J.D. from Widener University Delaware Law School, where he was a Dean’s List student and served as a Staff Editor on the Delaware Law Review.

After law school, he clerked for the Superior Court of New Jersey in Gloucester County, working in the Family Division. There, he gained experience with a wide range of matters, including juvenile cases, custody disputes, and domestic violence proceedings. He then served as an Assistant Prosecutor in Cumberland County, where he led the Bridgeton juvenile unit and worked on domestic violence-related weapons forfeiture cases. He also helped lead countywide initiatives focused on youth violence prevention and system reform.

In addition to his work in public service, Randall has experience in private practice and in complex litigation support. He has worked on civil and regulatory matters involving state agencies, antitrust enforcement, and environmental justice, and many other topics.

He is admitted to practice law in New Jersey and lives in South Jersey, where he works remotely and enjoys music, the beach, and spending time with family.

attorneys.name: Michael Brusca
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Negligence Lawyers in Ewing, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Since 2009, Michael has focused the majority of his practice on representing vulnerable people and their families when there is abuse or neglect in nursing homes, assisted living facilities, group homes, and hospitals.

Michael knows how to go to trial when necessary. He was lead counsel on the Estate of Mary Dwyer v. Harborview, the largest nursing home verdict in the state of New Jersey – a $13.2 million dollar verdict in Hudson County. He received great training serving as an Air Force Judge Advocate, where he tried many cases all over the world in the United States, Japan, Qatar, and Kuwait.

As one of the few who concentrates in this area, he regularly lectures around the country and teaches other lawyers how to prosecute these claims. He’s been published many times, including in the New Jersey Law Journal and the national attorney magazine Trial.

Having lost his own family members in institutions, Michael has a certain level of understanding with all of his clients. He knows first hand what it’s like to see someone you care about struggling, and brings a specific passion to his work.

Mr. Brusca is also a frequent contributor to the Nursing Home Law Blog.

attorneys.name: Hon. Peter A. Buchsbaum J.S.C. (Ret.)
attorneys.practice_type: Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Flemington, NJ
attorneys.bio:
The Honorable Peter A. Buchsbaum, J.S.C. (Ret.) joined the firm, Of Counsel with the firm in 2016, specializing in dispute resolution in land use matters, specifically concentrating on contests between developers and municipalities on issues concerning affordable housing.

Judge Buchsbaum's unmatched experience and scholarship in the field of land use are great assets to current and future clients of Lanza & Lanza LLP. His tenure as a practitioner, a Mayor and a jurist makes Judge Buchsbaum uniquely qualified to counsel clients attempting to reach fair resolutions to Mt. Laurel disputes and other land use matters.

Judge Buchsbaum was appointed as a judge of the Superior Court in 2004 and re-appointed in 2011. He was assigned to the Law Division, Civil Part and the Chancery Division, Family Part, sitting in Hunterdon County until his retirement in 2013. After his retirement, the New Jersey Supreme Court re-called Judge Buchsbaum to the bench part-time from July 2013 until April 2016, where he adjudicated land use disputes and served as Hunterdon County's probate judge. During his tenure on the bench, Judge Buchsbaum was designated the Mount Laurel Judge for Vicinage XIII, covering Hunterdon, Somerset and Warren Counties.

Prior to his appointment to the Superior Court, Judge Buchsbaum was a partner in a large Middlesex County law firm, where he represented both public and private sector clients. His practice concentrated on zoning and land use planning, Mt. Laurel housing, municipal law, state regulatory processes and environmental litigation. Judge Buchsbaum previously served as Mayor of the Township of West Amwell, was a member of the Township Committee and served as a member of the Township's Planning Board.

Judge Buchsbaum received his A. B. degree from Cornell University in 1967 and his J.D. from Harvard University in 1970. He began his legal career as law secretary to Joseph Weintraub, Chief Justice of the New Jersey Supreme Court. He and his wife, Elaine, live in West Amwell Township and have three adult children. He was honorably discharged from the United States Army Reserves in 1976.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Media Award, New Jersey Bar Association, 1987

Volunteer of the Year Hunterdon County Association for Retarded Citizens, 1987

Humanitarian of the Year, New Jersey Humane Society, 1987

attorneys.name: John M. Burke
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Jersey City, NJ
attorneys.bio:
John takes great pride in helping working men and women in New Jersey get back on their feet when they have been injured in an accident. He tells his clients to focus on getting better and he and his staff will take care of everything else.

John helped work his way through Law School by refereeing high school basketball and umpiring baseball games after classes would finish for the day. He also has run five marathons including a personal best time of 3:48 at the Philadelphia Marathon. John's lifelong love of sports, competition and teaching then led to years volunteering and coaching his children and other young boys and girls in basketball, baseball and softball in Montclair. John approaches his cases with the same competitive spirit that it takes to be successful in all things: hard work and preparation.

These are just some of his many excellent results for his clients:

Recently, John M. Burke, Esq. settled a products liability case for $4,500,000. It is believed to be one of the largest personal injury settlements or recoveries of the year in the State of New Jersey. The claim was brought on behalf of a worker who was permanently injured due to an allegedly defective product. John’s client underwent an above-the-knee amputation of the leg. The worker was not able to return to work given the severity of these injuries. The product manufacturer denied that its product was defective and denied that the product caused the accident. The case settled at a second mediation session before a retired Superior Court Judge. John and his team worked tirelessly for their client. The insurance carrier for the product manufacturer disputed liability. The case settled for more than twenty-two (22x) the insurance carrier’s initial offer of only $200,000. John invested significant resources and countless hours into building the case. John and his expert engineer had to inspect and test the machinery many times; John took depositions of witnesses to the accident, and of employees of the manufacturer. John also hired other persuasive expert witnesses to document the accident’s devastating effect on his client’s life. John hired economists to document the worker’s financial losses; vocational experts to meet and test the injured worker to see whether they could resume a less physically-demanding job; and medical experts to document the severity of these injuries and limitations. John also hired a videographer to document the most difficult days of his client’s life post-accident. John noted that “much of the credit goes to my client, who was not bitter even though their life took a tragic turn through no fault of their own. This client’s positive spirit assisted us greatly to obtain this excellent financial recovery for the client. Nothing will make up for what happened, but their financial future is now secure.” John understands that devastating injuries happen too often at work. He and his team strive to achieve justice for clients who have been badly injured through no fault of their own.

In 2020, John settled a case for $1,000,000 for a woman who was injured in two separate accidents. One was an auto accident in which she hurt her neck, back and hip, and then a fall-down accident in which she re-aggravated those parts of her body when she fell on ice in a parking lot. John was able to obtain security image of her falling in the parking lot and had medical illustrations to show the several surgeries she had to undergo. The defense argued that her injuries were preexisting as she had an earlier back surgery twenty years earlier. However, the case was strengthened with good visual evidence of her prior good health and activity in the years before her motor vehicle accident. The case resolved after successful mediation with a retired New Jersey Judge.

In 2018, John obtained a $1,250,000. settlement for a man injured by a tractor trailer accident while he was working at a garbage facility. The accident victim sustained injuries to his foot, jaw, shoulder and back. Initially, the insurance carriers for all involved completely denied responsibility for the man’s injuries. Even the worker's compensation carrier tried to not pay the immediate and urgent care he needed. John got that part resolved quickly and then took on the case against the insurance carriers for the people that caused the accident. John was able to get the case settled for the injured worker. By using his twenty years of experience in handling accident cases throughout the State of New Jersey and hiring qualified expert witnesses to be able to explain to a jury (and insurance company representatives) why a truck driver and a facility operator were at fault for this worker’s injuries, John was able to obtain this good settlement for his Client. This case also settled after a mediation session with a retired New Jersey Judge.

Mr. Burke obtained a significant recovery for a nineteen year old woman who was significantly injured in a motor vehicle accident. The young lady sustained herniated discs in her lower back and in her neck and a jaw (TMJ) injury. She underwent back surgery about two years after the accident as well as arthroscopic surgery for her jaw. The insurance carrier for the other driver contested that her injuries were related to the motor vehicle accident. The case arbitrated for the said amount which was paid by the insurance company.

Knowing what cases are worth are a very important trait for a personal injury lawyer so he can give good advice to his client when money is offered to settle. One of Mr. Burke's favorite cases was when he won a jury verdict for an injured client, a United States Marshall Officer, who fell and sustained a non-displaced broken ankle while transporting a prisoner through a parking lot on an uneven surface. The Plaintiff wore a cast for six weeks and then underwent physical therapy to help rehabilitate the ankle. Even though an offer was made, John and his client rejected it as being too low. Evidence was presented at trial that the injuries impeded the Plaintiff from engaging in rigorous physical activity, including special training in the United States Army Reserve. The jury award him double the offer from the insurance company. John and his client were pleased that the jury agreed that his case was worth that amount, which was in line with what John thought the case should settle for.

attorneys.name: Tyler J. Burrell
attorneys.practice_type: Employment and Labor Lawyers in Marlton, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Burrell is an Associate Attorney and Chief Operating Officer at McOmber McOmber & Luber. Mr. Burrell's legal practice focus in areas of employment law, class actions, and business litigation. Mr. Burrell's "leave no stone unturned" attitude and astute attention to detail allows him to provide exceptional service for clients. During his time at McOmber McOmber & Luber, he has assisted with numerous discrimination, retaliation, and whistleblower matters. Recently, Mr. Burrell helped prosecute a multi-state wage and hour class actions on behalf of Tastykate drivers, which resulted in a $3.15 million settlement to resolve minimum wage and overtime claims.

In addition to practicing law, Mr. Burrell is the firm's Chief Operating Officer. In this role, Mr. Burrell oversees the day-to-day operational and support functions of the firm, while also steering the firm's the long-range strategies and development. Mr. Burrell's responsibilities include refining processes to ensure efficiencies, implementing infrastructure and system changes - all with the mission of improving client services. In addition, Mr. Burrell oversees the Marketing Department.

Mr. Burrell's has had his hand on the pulse of firm's operations for years. He first joined the firm's Marlton office in 2017, focusing on business management and marketing through an externship program with Rowan University Rohrer College of Business. After the conclusion of his semester externship, he never left the team.

Mr. Burrell earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 2021. Through PENN's cross-disciplinary approach, Mr. Burrell also studied at Fels Institute of Government at the University of Pennsylvania, earning a Certificate in Politics. In law school, he focused his study on complex litigation, class actions, and advanced Federal Civil Procedure issues. Moreover, Mr. Burrell was a pro-bono researcher for the New Jersey Partners For Women and Justice, which offers free legal assistance to survivors of domestic violence. Mr. Burrell graduated summa cum laude from Rowan University with a bachelor's degree in Business Administration. Before Rowan, Mr. Burrell attended Rowan College at Burlington County through the NJ STARS program.

Mr. Burrell currently serves as Council President (Councilman At-Large) of his hometown, Delran, New Jersey. Mr. Burrell serves as one of the youngest-elected officials and Council President in the State of New Jersey, first elected to office at the age of 19. As a two-term Councilman, he used his age and vigor to bring a new perspective and engagement to his community. During his tenure, Mr. Burrell pioneered transparency, modernized government services, and planned large-scale community events.

Mr. Burrell currently serves as a Board of Education Member on the joint Board of the Burlington County Special Services School District & Burlington County Institute of Technology.

Mr. Burrell's success in building a stronger and diverse community has been widely recognized, as he earned a place on NJ Insider's Millennials To Watch List in 2020, 2019, & 2018. He also earned the distinction of "30 Under 30 Trendsetters" by SNJ Millennials - an award honoring those who have committed to serving their communities.

attorneys.name: Albert Buzzetti
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Englewood Cliffs, NJ
attorneys.bio:
ALBERT LOUIS BUZZETTI was born in Bronx, New York. He attended the University Miami and the University of L'Aquila in L'Aquila, Italy. Albert graduated from the University of Miami in 3.5 years and completed his law degree at Pace University School of Law in 1993.

During law school, Albert worked for in-house counsel on a variety of areas of law including environmental litigation, contracts, insurance coverage disputes and international arbitration disputes. Immediately thereafter, Albert commenced a one year term as the Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable Patrick F.X. Fitzpatrick of the Superior Court of New Jersey. Albert prepared legal opinions on a variety of complex civil matters including insurance coverage cases, employment cases, contract cases, zoning appeals and summary judgment motions.

In 1995, Albert commenced working in the private sector where he immediately began handling a wide variety of personal injury, commercial litigation and transactional matters.

During his years of practice, Albert gained valuable experience and built a strong base of clients, both corporate and individual. In 1998, Albert became a co-managing partner of Sekas & Buzzetti, L.L.C. In 2003, Albert formed Albert Buzzetti & Associates, L.L.C., which consists of four attorneys and seven full time paralegals. Albert's clients include personal injury plaintiffs, banks, real estate developers, residential buyers and sellers and municipalities.

Albert is fluent in Italian and conversational in Spanish and, as a result, Albert Buzzetti & Associates, L.L.C. has attracted a large number of clients who speak Italian and/or Spanish as their first language.

attorneys.name: Stephen J Caccavale
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law (Commercial Transactions and Litigation) Lawyers in Red Bank, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Caccavale is senior counsel with the firm. He was born in Belleville, New Jersey. He graduated from Bethany College with a B.A. in Economics. Mr. Caccavale graduated from Rutgers University with a Master of Business Administration (concentrating in finance). He graduated from Seton Hall University School of Law with a J.D. and was admitted to the New Jersey Bar and U.S. District Court, District of New Jersey in 1990; and the Florida Bar in 2007.

Mr. Cacccavale’s business background includes employment as a financial analyst for corporate executive management for a national corporation, and as a product development financial analyst for a retail management consulting company. He also worked in the accounting field with a national accounting firm in the areas of estate and trust administration and taxation. Mr. Caccavale has also served as a financial consultant to the Rutgers University Small Business Development Center in Newark, New Jersey.

Mr. Caccavale began his legal career at Horn, Kaplan, Goldberg, Gorny, and Daniels, PA in Atlantic City, New Jersey in the firm’s commercial transaction department. He represented debtors, creditors, and creditor committees through bankruptcy reorganizations and receivership proceedings with LaPenna, Teitelbaum & Caccavale, P.C. in Clifton, New Jersey. Mr. Caccavale was a partner at Teitelbaum & Caccavale, PC in Bloomfield, NJ where he concentrated his practice in commercial and corporate law, estate planning and administration, and bankruptcy and insolvency law. Prior to coming to the firm Mr. Caccavale was a partner at Rudolph & Kayal, PA in Manasquan, New Jersey continuing his areas of practice in commercial transactions, business litigation, and trusts and estates.

Mr. Caccavale concentrates his practice in the areas of business law (commercial transactions and litigation); trust and estate law (estate planning and estate administration), real estate, and elder law.

attorneys.name: Donald A. Caminiti
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation - General Negligence Lawyers in Hackensack, NJ
attorneys.bio:
The practice of representing victims of negligence hasn't changed dramatically over all these years. We're still trying to help grievously injured people get on their feet again. What has changed is there is now a concerted effort by the insurance industry to discredit the jury system. A lot of money has been spent by the wrongdoers lobby to promote the idea that a jury composed of ordinary citizens, a jury of one's peers, is somehow incapable of making a sound reasoned judgment.

Many people see attorneys in a courtroom and marvel at their presentation, their skills and oratory. But the fact is there is much, much preparation behind the courtroom drama. Someone once said there are no lions in the courtroom, just drudges back at the office. There are plenty of 12-hour days, and lots of pressure in preparing a case for trial.

I have worked on many difficult cases in which a dangerous manufacturer, a negligent doctor or a careless driver caused an injury. Some of those cases have taken years to resolve, but we've been able to do what's right and what's in the best interest of our client. Unfortunately, many of those cases are settled with confidentiality agreements, so we can't disclose the problem that caused the accident and injury in the first place. That is unfortunate. Society would be much better off if we abolished confidentiality agreements so that the wrongdoer's conduct could be exposed for all to see.

My work has garnered considerable recognition. I have ranked in the top-10 five times previously, as well as 7 inclusions to the top-100.

I enjoy what I do - working within our civil justice system to help obtain for my clients a fair and just resolution of their case.

attorneys.name: Donald F. Campbell Sr.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills, Trusts, Estates Lawyers in Jackson, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Judge Campbell was born in Temple, Texas in 1943 where his father was a career Army Officer and grew up living in Germany, Japan, Texas, New York, Georgia and North Carolina. He graduated from Archbishop Molloy H.S. in New York City and then attended Seton Hall University in South Orange, N.J. where he obtained both his BA in Sociology and a commission as a 2nd Lieutenant in the U.S. Army. He then attended Seton Hall Law School, graduating in 1968. Upon passing the N.J. Bar exam and after attending the U.S. Army Infantry and Intelligence Schools, he served a one-year tour of duty in Vietnam.

Judge Campbell opened his own law practice in Jackson, New Jersey in 1972 after working in Lakewood for just over two years. During the next ten years, he was named as Ocean County's Inheritance Tax Supervisor; the attorney for the Jackson Township Board of Health, the Lacey Township Municipal Utilities Authority, a number of Boards of Fire Commissioners; as Municipal Court Judge for the Borough of Island Heights and as an acting Municipal Court Judge in Lakehurst, Lakewood and South Toms River.

Governor Brendan Byrne appointed Judge Campbell to the Superior Court in January of 1982 where he served in the Family, Criminal and Civil Divisions. Beginning in 1994, he was also privileged to sit in Burlington County for approximately three years in both Civil and Family Courts.

For over forty years, Judge Campbell has also served our nation in the U.S. Army ultimately rising to the rank of Major General in the U.S. Army Reserves. His assignments included four years as Commander of the U.S. Army's Civil Affairs and Psychological Operations Command, six months where he was assigned to work in Iraq and Turkey (Operation Provide Comfort), five months in Haiti (he was the senior Advisor to the Ministry of Justice) and most recently, six months in Iraq (again as Senior Advisor to the Ministry of Justice).

Judge Campbell has received numerous awards over his career. Most recently he was honored as a 2016 inaugural inductee into the United States Army Reserve Officers' Training Corps National Hall of Fame. He also received the 2016 Alumni Hall of Fame award from the Seton Hall University ROTC. The West Point Association of New Jersey also recognized him recently for his combined service to both the Judiciary and our nation. In 2009, the Jackson Chamber of Commerce honored him as a "Citizen of the Year." He also received "the 1995 Award of Merit" from the American Judges Association for his work in Haiti.

In 1965, Judge Campbell married the former Michele Ray. They have five children and thirteen grandchildren.

attorneys.name: E. Gregory M. Cannarozzi Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of E. Gregory M. Cannarozzi
attorneys.practice_type: DWI Lawyers in Oradell, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Whom you choose to represent you in your traffic, criminal, TRO, defense case will have an enormous impact on the outcome. Even for a first offense, penalties associated with traffic violations can include license suspension, substantial fines, mandatory attendance at a State or NJMVC approved alcohol program (if charged with DUI/DWI) and probation-diversion. Recently, the laws regarding DWI and DUID as well as cannabis possession have drastically changed in New Jersey. Although a Defendant is never entitled to a jury trial, In certain situations, plea bargaining is now permitted in New Jersey. New York laws are completely different and there can be multiple legal implications for certain offenses with carry over from each State. Plea bargaining in certain alcohol and drug related driving offenses is now permitted in New Jersey. However, there are no jury trials on DWI and DUID NJ offenses despite the exposure in certain circumstances to 180 days of incarceration in the county jail. Attorney E. Gregory M. Cannarozzi is experienced, skillful, trial tested and dedicated to your defense, and will fight for your rights every step of the way.

The same level of dedication is provided in all areas of NJ Personal Injury cases by my law-firm. Experienced trial lawyers generally obtain optimum monetary results for their clients, and the rewards which I have achieved for my injured clients, which includes auto, truck, premises, slip and fall, traumatic brain injury, biking and dog bite cases are accurately reflected in their business reviews of my representation. Free consultation is always provided.

SPECIAL AGENCIES: New Jersey Association of Professional Mediators; Commerce and Industry of New Jersey; UNICO.

Honors

Excellence in Legal Writing Award from Bridgeport School of Law

attorneys.name: Natalie Cardona Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Hackensack, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Natalie Cardona is an accomplished attorney specializing in family law and licensed to practice in both New Jersey and New York. She obtained her Juris Doctor degree from Pace University School of Law in 2014, following her graduation from Montclair State University in 2010.

Natalie’s passion for the law developed at a young age, fueled by her desire to make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. Her practice primarily focuses on family law, encompassing a wide range of issues such as divorce, child custody, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, name changes, and cases involving the Division of Child Protection and Permanency (DCP&P). Natalie approaches cases with empathy and understanding, taking the trust her clients place in her very seriously. She recognizes the emotional challenges her clients face and is committed to using her legal knowledge and experience to support her clients and achieve the best possible outcomes.

Natalie serves as the Co-Chair of the Family Law Committee, demonstrating her dedication to staying current with evolving legal trends and passion for providing the highest level of legal expertise. As a member of the Hudson County Bar Association and the New Jersey State Bar Association, she enjoys fostering connections and professional relationships that enhance her ability to advocate for her clients.

Born in Israel and raised in New Jersey, Natalie is fluent in Hebrew, enabling her to assist clients from diverse backgrounds with their family law matters.

Natalie believes it is a privilege to advise clients on their legal rights and takes pride in offering practical options to work toward favorable resolutions. She is dedicated to providing compassionate, knowledgeable, and effective legal representation, ensuring her clients receive the guidance they need during their legal proceedings.

attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Mt. Laurel, NJ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Carlson's practice concentrates on the defense of New Jersey and Pennsylvania personal injury matters on behalf of insurance companies, self-insured entities and third-party administrators in the fields of premises liability, transportation law, and construction claims. He has also handled commercial, insurance coverage, fire loss, trucking accident, Dram Shop, subrogation and first party "Personal Injury Protection " (PIP) matters, as well as Hazmat rapid response services to trucking accidents.

Mr. Carlson is a Certified by the Supreme Court of New Jersey as a Civil Trial Attorney. This designation, held by less than 3% of New Jersey attorneys, requires a rigorous application process demonstrating trial experience, peer and judicial references, passage of a written examination, and continuing legal education, with re-certification required every five years.

Mr. Carlson is a member of both the New Jersey and Pennsylvania bars. He has handled matters in all of New Jersey's 21 counties, Philadelphia, Court of Common Pleas, and in each Federal vicinage.

Mr. Carlson has periodically presented both written and oral seminars to clients and industry organizations on topics and recent developments in case law in many of these practice areas.
